target.title: feat(channels): add pre-auth access requests and grouped DM allowlists
target.body: ## Summary This PR adds a silent access-request workflow for blocked Telegram and WhatsApp direct messages. - Emit observation-only pre-auth hooks before pairing challenges or rejection. - Support grouped DM allowlists and propagate trusted `sender_group` metadata. - Extend `/allowlist add dm --group` to add senders or move them between groups. - Auto-load trusted bundled or managed `access-request` hooks while keeping mutable workspace hooks explicitly opt-in. - Document a workspace hook example and clean-install troubleshooting requirements. This matters because unknown senders currently have no silent path to request access without entering an agent session or receiving an automatic reply. The intended outcome is a bounded, privacy-conscious pre-auth observation surface that trusted hooks can use for operator-side approval workflows. Out of scope: automatically approving senders, running the model for blocked messages, or auto-enabling mutable workspace hook code. Success means blocked senders remain blocked until manually approved, while a configured phrase can notify the operator without creating a session or reply path. Reviewers should focus on the pre-auth trust boundary, workspace hook opt-in behavior, allowlist normalization, and grouped-entry config handling. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? N/A - no linked issue. Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? N/A. Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No known maintainer or owner request. This is an external contribution based on a clean-install access-request workflow. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Unknown Telegram and WhatsApp DM senders can silently request manual access without creating an agent session, running the model, or receiving a reply. - Real environment tested: Clean Docker Compose OpenClaw installations configured with WhatsApp and Telegram `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and an explicitly enabled workspace `access-request` hook. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Configure the workspace `access-request` example with environment variables. 2. Run `openclaw config set tools.profile messaging`. 3. Run `openclaw config set commands.config true`. 4. Recreate the container with `docker compose down && docker compose up -d`. 5. Send the configured access phrase from a blocked WhatsApp number. 6. Approve the sender from the operator chat with `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp --group restricted `. - Evidence after fix: 1. WhatsApp blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 2. Operator receives the silent WhatsApp access request notification. 3. WhatsApp sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp`. 4. WhatsApp admitted sender receives a normal agent response. 5. Telegram blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 6. Operator receives the silent Telegram access request notification. 7. Telegram sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel telegram`. - Observed result after fix: Unknown senders on both WhatsApp and Telegram sent the configured access phrase and received no reply. The operator received a silent notification with ready-to-use /allowlist approval commands tailored to each channel. After approval, the sender was admitted to the restricted group. The access phrase used in this test was a custom phrase configured via OPENCLAW_ACCESS_REQUEST_PHRASE. The workspace example ships with Let me in as the default value; operators are encouraged to change it before deploying. - What was not tested: Multi-account deployments were not tested live. - Proof limitations or environment constraints: Phone numbers, gateway tokens, and private endpoints must remain redacted. - Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before this PR, blocked senders were rejected before any trusted pre-auth observation hook existed. ## Tests and validation Commands run: ```bash node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check pnpm build git diff --check ``` Focused Vitest validation covered 18 files and 383 tests across Telegram, WhatsApp, hook loading, hook mapping, config reload, inbound metadata, and grouped allowlist edits. Focused Vitest command: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/channel.allowlist.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/dm-access.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/inbound-context.contract.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-accessors.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/access-control.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/process-message.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-allowlist.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/allowlist-config-edit.test.ts src/hooks/internal-hooks.test.ts src/hooks/loader.test.ts src/hooks/message-hook-mappers.test.ts src/plugins/wired-hooks-message.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts ``` WhatsApp E2E validation: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply.web-auto-reply.connection-and-logging.e2e.test.ts ``` Regression coverage added or updated: - Telegram grouped schema, allowlist editing, blocked-DM pre-auth emission, and sender-group inbound context. - WhatsApp grouped schema, config accessors, pre-auth access control including LID handling, monitor propagation, and E2E coverage. - Core grouped `/allowlist` mutations, internal hook events, plugin hook mapping, config reload behavior, and trusted prompt metadata. Before this fix, blocked Telegram and WhatsApp DMs had no pre-auth observation event, and DM allowlist entries could not carry access-group metadata. ## Risk checklist Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. The config schema adds optional grouped DM `allowFrom` entries. Existing string entries remain supported. No migration is required. Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. What is the highest-risk area? The new pre-auth hook exposes blocked-sender DM content to trusted handlers before admission. How is that risk mitigated? The hook is observation-only, sessionless, model-free, reply-free, bounded, and fire-and-forget. Mutable workspace hooks remain explicitly opt-in. Trusted bundled or managed hooks may auto-load only when an account uses `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`. Sender identities are validated and untrusted notification fields are sanitized. ## Current review state What is the next action? Submit for maintainer review. What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof? CI and maintainer review pending. Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed? Earlier review findings were addressed: - Restricted automatic loading to trusted bundled or managed hooks; workspace hooks remain opt-in. - Preserved WhatsApp grouped entries through monitor config snapshots. - Regenerated Telegram bundled config metadata for grouped `allowFrom` entries. ## Agent Transcripts Two redacted English reviewer artifacts are available: - [Curated implementation transcript summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28520597/openclaw-pre-auth-agent-transcript.en.md) — recommended for a quick review. - [Full translated implementation transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28520607/openclaw-pre-auth-agent-transcript.full.en.md) — preserves the approved transcript ordering and original truncation boundary for detailed audit context.

target.title: fix(discord): retry stale preview cleanup after final delivery
target.body:
Closes #104865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord users with partial streaming could see a stale preview beside the fresh final reply when preview cleanup failed transiently.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preview ownership is now cleared only after DELETE succeeds. Discord teardown performs one bounded cleanup retry when a fresh final was delivered but an unfinalized preview ID remains; previews finalized in place are still preserved.

This keeps retry policy at the existing lifecycle boundaries. It does not add timers, configuration, background queues, or additional final-message sends.

## User Impact

Transient Discord preview cleanup failures get one recovery attempt during normal turn teardown instead of immediately becoming unrecoverable stale messages. Final replies are still delivered exactly once.

Mattermost uses the shared helper and now also retains failed preview IDs for a later cleanup call.

## Evidence

### RED → GREEN

- Shared lifecycle regressions:
  - first DELETE rejects;
  - preview ID remains owned;
  - second clear retries DELETE and clears ownership on success;
  - if ownership advances while the old DELETE is in flight, compare-and-clear preserves the replacement preview ID.
- Discord process regression:
  - fresh final delivery succeeds once;
  - first preview clear retains the ID;
  - teardown invokes one second clear;
  - preview ID is then cleared.

Both tests failed on current `main` (`9a04fb40ce`) for the expected reasons before the implementation changes, then passed afterward.

### Live Discord proof

Redacted live run on exact head `5582df93dfe17ac4ec3d8c39dc3d9a857a9f5bf5`: [Crabbox run `run_4627a4bad139`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_4627a4bad139).

- Isolated public-network Crabbox; no instance role, Tailscale, or hydrated credentials.
- Created a real Discord preview successfully.
- Replaced only the first preview DELETE response with a controlled HTTP 500; the preview ID remained owned.
- Delivered exactly one real final Discord reply.
- Teardown made exactly one retry; that DELETE reached Discord.
- After cleanup, live Discord GET returned 404 for the preview and 200 for the final reply.
- The final reply was then deleted by the harness cleanup block.

The evidence omits credentials, broker data, guild/channel/application/message IDs, and message content. The first 500 is controlled fault injection because a transient Discord 5xx cannot be requested deterministically; the retry and both postconditions are live Discord API results.

Accessible redacted diagnostic manifest (also emitted by the linked run):

target.title: feat(agent): preserve interrupted-turn context and anchor session recall on search hits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two long-session truthfulness/recall gaps, found by a structured survey of leading agent-runtime internals (designs ported, no code copied):

1. **Aborted turns lie by omission.** After `/stop` or steering aborts a tool-running turn, the transcript records only an empty aborted assistant message. The next provider request carries no signal that tools may have partially executed, so the model assumes clean completion and repeats or skips side-effecting work. Codex CLI ships a `<turn_aborted>` context fragment for exactly this (`codex-rs/core/src/context/turn_aborted.rs`).
2. **Search hits are dead ends.** `sessions_search` returns a stable `messageId`, but `sessions_history` can only tail/offset-page, so a hit buried in an older (or pre-reset archived) session cannot be reopened in one call. The fix is anchoring a bounded window around the hit id.

Closes #105828. Closes #105829.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both fixes serve one story: long-running multi-turn work should stay truthful when interrupted and recoverable when searched.

- **Interrupted-turn truth** (`packages/agent-core`): abort paths (loop abort, loop failure, agent failure, harness failure) append a hidden `openclaw:turn-aborted` custom message — except clean turn handoffs: `sessions_yield` now aborts with a `turnHandoff: true` reason and agent-core skips the guidance for those, so a deliberate yield is never mislabeled as an interruption (this also keeps subagent announce turns byte-clean; caught by the `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` QA scenario). It is normalized to a user-role text message immediately before provider conversion, so the model sees the guidance on the next turn while channel-visible history stays clean. Append-only, preserving prompt-cache prefixes.
- **Anchored session recall** (`sessions_history` + `chat.history`): the tool accepts a search hit's `sessionId` + `messageId`, validates session ownership, and the gateway reads one anchor-centered page from a single stable transcript snapshot (active or reset-archive), byte-capped by growing around the anchor. Anchored responses deliberately expose no offset cursor/pagination metadata: numeric offsets cannot encode which archived transcript the anchor resolved to, so handing one out would corrupt subsequent paging. This composes with #105688's offset paging — anchored reads are a separate `pagination`-less arm of the same `readChatHistoryPage` gate, and CLI-import-bound sessions fall through to the full-snapshot merge where the handler-level cap still centers on the anchor.

## User Impact

- After stopping or steering mid-run, the agent checks state instead of assuming aborted commands completed (or silently duplicating them).
- Cross-session recall becomes one-step: search, then reopen the surrounding conversation directly, including sessions archived by `/new`.

## Evidence

- Real-runtime gateway proof on the final head (SHA in the proof comments) (Blacksmith Testbox, Linux Node 24: built gateway process, real WS protocol client, real session store + SQLite FTS; scripted OpenAI-compatible provider so request payloads are ground truth): (a) abort a held-open turn via `chat.abort`, follow-up provider request contains the interruption/partial-execution guidance; (b) bury an anchor behind seven later turns, confirm the tail omits it, find it via live SQLite FTS, reopen a five-message neighborhood by `sessionId` + `messageId` with no offset cursor exposed.
- New behavior tests: agent-loop abort marker paths, anchored/`sessionId` validation and windowing in `sessions-history-tool` + gateway protocol, anchored `chat.history` (bounded page, reset-archive anchor, offset+messageId rejection, foreign `sessionId` rejection).
- Affected sweep (agent-core, gateway-protocol, sessions tools, transcript readers, gateway chat, config/sessions) green after rebase onto `main` (post-#105688 offset-paging integration; anchored reads are a separate pagination-less arm of the same read gate); `tsgo` lanes green; `check:changed` lanes green incl. Plugin SDK API baseline regen; protocol schema + Swift models and prompt snapshots regenerated; SDK surface budgets unchanged; fresh autoreview clean. Full verdict JSON in the proof comment below.

target.title: feat(memory): add multi-slot memory role architecture
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a memory-plugin architecture flaw: OpenClaw currently has one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner even though the product, docs, bundled plugins, and runtime behavior already treat “memory” as several different responsibilities.

Today, factual recall, auto-capture, compaction, dreaming/consolidation, and user/session modeling are all forced through the same global selector. That makes documented memory stacks impossible or brittle: selecting one memory provider can unintentionally displace another provider that owns a different responsibility.

This PR corrects that mismatch by introducing purpose-specific memory role slots:

- `memory.recall`
- `memory.capture`
- `memory.compaction`
- `memory.dreaming`
- `memory.userModel`

The new role slots are the mechanism. The fix is that OpenClaw can now represent the memory architecture it already documents and partially implements.

## What Problem This Solves

This is a flaw fix, not just a feature request.

OpenClaw’s memory ecosystem is already multi-role:

- `memory-core` / QMD provide local factual recall/search over project memory, session transcripts, and Markdown/QMD corpora.
- Honcho provides cross-session user, agent, and session modeling.
- LanceDB provides embedding-backed long-term recall and auto-capture.
- Active Memory orchestrates recall before generation by using whichever provider owns recall.
- Memory Wiki compiles durable memory into a companion knowledge vault rather than replacing active memory.
- Dreaming/consolidation is a separate runtime responsibility from ordinary recall.

The current `plugins.slots.memory` contract cannot express that architecture. It treats every `kind: "memory"` provider as competing for one owner slot, even when the providers are designed to do different jobs. That leads to three concrete problems:

1. **Documented combinations are not representable.** Configs such as builtin/QMD recall + Honcho user modeling, LanceDB capture + local recall, or Active Memory over a selected recall provider cannot be modeled cleanly through one memory owner.
2. **Runtime behavior depends on exceptions and side paths.** Plugins that should compose have to rely on context-engine ownership, sidecar behavior, fallback logic, or plugin-specific handling instead of a shared contract.
3. **Diagnostics and lifecycle handling become misleading.** Startup, validation, status, doctor repair, skill publishing, uninstall cleanup, runtime memory resolution, and SDK-facing aliases need to know which provider owns which memory responsibility.

So while this PR adds new public config keys, the intent is corrective: make the config/runtime contract match the memory system OpenClaw already exposes.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

After this PR, OpenClaw can express memory stacks that were previously documented or implied but not cleanly configurable:

- `memory-core` or QMD can own factual recall while Honcho owns user/session modeling.
- LanceDB can own recall and/or capture without forcing unrelated memory roles through the same selector.
- Active Memory can use the configured `memory.recall` provider instead of depending on hard-coded assumptions.

PR #88504 closes that product/docs/runtime gap by replacing the single memory owner with explicit role slots — `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel` — while preserving legacy `memory` as a recall shorthand, so the documented memory-plugin interop story becomes actually representable in config and runtime behavior.

- Adds per-agent memory role-slot overrides under `agents.list[*].plugins.slots`, limited to memory roles plus legacy `memory`.

- Preserves the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` path for LosslessClaw and other context-engine plugins.
- Explicitly rejects unsupported per-agent `agents.list[*].plugins.slots.contextEngine` overrides because agent-scoped context-engine semantics are outside this PR.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds `src/plugins/slot-resolution.ts` as the shared role-slot helper layer for canonical memory role keys, defaults, normalization, effective per-agent resolution, and configured selection collection.
- Updates config schema/types/help/labels/docs for global and per-agent memory role slots.
- Keeps `PluginSlotsConfig.contextEngine` for global plugin slots, and adds an agent-slot type/schema that omits `contextEngine`.
- Updates doctor legacy memory-slot handling so `doctor --fix` canonicalizes to `memory.recall` while retaining legacy `memory` during the compatibility window.
- Updates plugin loader/activation/startup resolution so explicit role-slot selections activate memory plugins without confusing default `memory-core` fallback with a user-selected plugin under restrictive allowlists.
- Extends validation to report missing role-slot plugin refs and validate schemas for plugins selected only by non-recall or per-agent memory roles.
- Extends skill publishing, status scanning, uninstall cleanup, memory runtime, dreaming, compaction provider, and SDK alias behavior to use the role-aware model.
- Keeps memory runtime registrations addressable by plugin id, so runtime recall dispatch follows the resolved global or per-agent `memory.recall` owner.
- Passes the session agent id into Pi embedded extension factory construction so safeguard compaction provider selection honors per-agent `memory.compaction` overrides in both normal session runs and manual/queued compaction paths.
- Updates bundled memory plugin manifests/docs to describe role support and the recall shorthand migration.

target.title: fix(agents): tighten grepSchema context/limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105822

**Problem**: `grepSchema.context` and `grepSchema.limit` use `Type.Number`, accepting fractional values like `1.5` or `10.5` that are semantically invalid for context lines and match counts.

**Solution**: Change both fields to `Type.Integer` so schema validation rejects floats before reaching tool logic. Export `grepSchema` from the module so tests validate against the production schema instead of a reconstructed copy. This follows the same pattern applied to the `ls` tool schema in PR #105827.

**What changed**: Two characters in `src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.ts:44-49` — `Type.Number` → `Type.Integer` for both `context` and `limit`. The test now imports and validates against the exported production `grepSchema`. Removed standalone `_validate_grep.mjs` script from repo root. Rebased branch onto latest upstream/main to resolve branch-behind-main status.

**NOT changed**: Tool execution behavior, default values (context=0, limit=100), `normalizePositiveLimit` clamping, any other schema field, or tool registration. Existing grep tests continue to pass. The standalone `_validate_grep.mjs` script was removed as redundant — the production schema test covers the same ground.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Schema-level rejection of float `context` and `limit` values via the production `grepSchema`.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.limit-schema.test.ts` then direct schema validation via `node --import tsx/esm`
**After-fix evidence**: Test + terminal output both pass (see Tests and terminal output below).
**Observed result after the fix**: `Check(grepSchema, { pattern: "foo", context: 1.5, limit: 50 })` returns `false`; `Check(grepSchema, { pattern: "foo", context: 3, limit: 10.5 })` returns `false`. All four validation scenarios pass as shown in the terminal output below.
**What was not tested**: End-to-end grep execution (covered by existing `grep.stream-errors.test.ts`); real OpenClaw agent runtime integration is out of scope for this schema-level gate.

## Tests and validation

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.limit-schema.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 RUN  v4.1.9

 ✓ |unit-fast| rejects float context and limit — validates against production grepSchema

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)

$ node --import tsx/esm -e "..."

  PASS {"pattern":"foo","context":3,"limit":50} → true
  PASS {"pattern":"foo","context":1.5,"limit":50} → false
  PASS {"pattern":"foo","context":3,"limit":10.5} → false
  PASS {"pattern":"foo"} → true
4/4 passed
```

Validated against the exported production `grepSchema`:

| Input | Expected | Result |
|-------|----------|--------|
| `{ pattern: "foo", context: 3, limit: 50 }` | ✅ accept | passed |
| `{ pattern: "foo", context: 1.5, limit: 50 }` | ❌ reject (float context) | passed |
| `{ pattern: "foo", context: 3, limit: 10.5 }` | ❌ reject (float limit) | passed |
| `{ pattern: "foo" }` (optionals omitted) | ✅ accept | passed |

The branch was rebased onto the latest upstream/main to resolve the stale-base issue flagged in the initial review.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — integers previously accepted by `Type.Number` remain accepted by `Type.Integer`
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — production schema validated directly
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation — schema is self-documenting via TypeBox types
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

target.title: fix(memory): accept leading-zero Content-Length on JSON responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where remote memory provider calls would reject successful JSON responses when the provider returned a valid decimal `Content-Length` header with leading zeros, such as `00017`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory-host SDK bounded JSON response reader now accepts digit-only `Content-Length` values while still rejecting empty, non-decimal, and unsafe integer values. This keeps the fix inside the response-size guard used by `postJson` and batch file upload responses without changing request routing, auth, provider selection, or response body limits.

## User Impact

Remote memory and embedding workflows can parse successful JSON responses from providers that emit leading-zero content lengths, while malformed or oversized responses remain blocked at the same guard boundary.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: `postJson` and `uploadBatchJsonlFile` accept successful JSON responses with leading-zero `Content-Length` headers while preserving bounded response parsing.
- Current-head proof at `91b4b4062cbf3f0b85bdc6049a51a604ba5ba0f0`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/post-json.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/batch-upload.test.ts` passed with 2 shards and 15 tests.
- Diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the focused regressions parse `content-length: 0002` and `content-length: 00017` on successful JSON responses and return the expected `{}` payload and `file_123` upload id.

target.title: fix(agents): reject invalid bundled LSP framing
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: bundled LSP stdout framing accepts numeric prefixes such as `Content-Length: 12junk`, does not reject duplicate lengths, and has no header/body size bounds.
- Solution: parse the header boundary strictly and fail the affected LSP session immediately on the first framing violation.
- What changed: one runtime parser and its focused regression tests.
- What was not changed: outbound framing, bundle discovery/configuration, LSP request payloads, tool schemas, or the general request timeout.

## What Problem This Solves

The current regex is not anchored to a complete header value and `Number.parseInt` accepts a decimal prefix. A malformed frame can therefore be cut at the wrong byte boundary; an oversized unterminated header or declared body can also remain buffered indefinitely. Subsequent JSON-RPC responses no longer align with pending request ids, so users see a misleading generic 10-second timeout instead of the framing error.

## User Impact

A broken or adversarial bundled language server can stall every pending LSP tool request in its session and retain an ever-growing buffer. After this patch, the first invalid frame rejects pending requests with a specific LSP framing error and terminates the child process, while valid frames keep completing normally.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows / completes:** #85341, which internalized the bundled agent LSP runtime.
- **Gap this fills:** the internalized stdio parser still partially accepts malformed `Content-Length` values and lacks framing size limits.
- **Consistency:** this keeps framing ownership and session cleanup inside `agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`; no discovery or tool-contract layer is changed.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #103046.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** it overlaps on oversized bodies but does not reject suffixed or duplicate `Content-Length` fields or bound unterminated headers.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** it fails at the fatal header boundary without adding cross-chunk drain state, so pending requests receive the actual error immediately.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** the proof drives `createBundleLspToolRuntime` through a real spawned stdio executable that emits both the invalid frame and a canonical control frame.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** invalid child-process output currently becomes session stalls, retained buffers, and misleading timeouts.
- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility / session-state / availability.
- **Risk explanation:** protocol-invalid or over-limit frames that were previously partially accepted, skipped, or buffered now close the affected LSP session.
- **Why acceptable:** the intentional compatibility change is limited to invalid framing; valid chunked and multibyte frames retain the existing byte-oriented path, and both focused tests and a real subprocess control cover it.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — RED reproduces the permissive parser, the exact-head 18-test focused suite passes in sanitized AWS Crabbox, and the changed runtime path is exercised through both a real third-party language server and a malformed real subprocess.
- **Patch quality notes:** the production diff adds a broad `JSON.parse` catch only at the untrusted frame boundary; it narrows the caught value when formatting the terminal protocol error and does not swallow it. The related open PR scan found #103046 and is documented above. Automated large-diff/session/message warnings include unrelated commits that advanced `origin/main`; the actual three-dot PR diff is two files: the LSP runtime and its test.
- **Target test file:** `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts`.
- **Root cause:** the canonical stdout parser uses an unanchored `Content-Length` regex followed by `Number.parseInt`; because prefix parsing accepts `12junk` as `12`, the framing invariant is broken before bytes enter session state, and missing size bounds let incomplete declarations wait indefinitely.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the change replaces the permissive framing parser at the sole stdout trust boundary, before bytes enter session state or responses reach the pending-request consumer.
- **What did NOT change:** this patch changes only bundled LSP stdout parsing and its focused tests. It does not change public API, configuration schema, outbound protocol framing, provider/channel behavior, default LSP methods, unrelated session state, docs, formatting, or lockfiles.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts` is the canonical owner of bundled LSP stdio framing, buffer state, pending request settlement, and child cleanup. The invariant is enforced there once rather than downstream in each LSP tool.
- **Scenario locked in:** suffixed length, duplicate length, oversized declared body, and oversized unterminated header all fail immediately; a canonical frame still completes initialize/hover.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** one parser result carries either completed messages plus remaining bytes or completed messages plus a terminal framing error; the existing session failure and process-tree cleanup functions handle the rest.

## Evidence

- **Exact PR head:** `5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3`.
- **Environment:** sanitized direct AWS Crabbox, Linux / Node 24.15.0, public networking, no Tailscale, no hydration, immutable `--fresh-pr openclaw/openclaw#105460` checkout.
- **Focused suite:** Crabbox run `run_55379c4d977b` passed all 18 tests in `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts`, including manifest-registry reuse, valid `Content-Type`, colonless headers, duplicate/suffixed lengths, size bounds, chunking, request failure, and process cleanup.
- **Real third-party server:** Crabbox run `run_f805f238ea53` installed `typescript-language-server@5.3.0` with `typescript@5.9.3`, loaded it through a temporary enabled Claude bundle manifest/registry, spawned it through `createBundleLspToolRuntime`, and completed a canonical `textDocument/hover` through the resulting OpenClaw tool.
- **Malformed subprocess:** the same run loaded a second real Node child through the same bundle/runtime path. It returned a valid initialize response, then a hover response containing a colonless header line. The pending request rejected immediately with `LSP framing error: header line must contain a colon`, and the child recorded `SIGTERM`.
- **Boundary crossed:** bundle manifest/config and prepared manifest registry → embedded-agent LSP runtime → real OS process spawn → stdin JSON-RPC → stdout LSP framing → pending request settlement → process-tree termination.
- **Rebase integration:** the branch was rebased onto `origin/main` at `afb282ee682`; current main later advanced to `e9e7d385e013ef9dd0daba614a263d334f02eac0` without any intervening changes to either touched LSP file. Current-main manifest-registry plumbing remains present in the PR head.
- **Proof artifact:** the harness was temporary and uncommitted; it asserted the immutable checkout SHA before running and removed its bundle/server artifacts afterward.

```text
{
  "proof_sha": "5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3",
  "real_server": "typescript-language-server@5.3.0 + typescript@5.9.3",
  "canonical_hover": "completed through OpenClaw runtime",
  "malformed_header": "LSP framing error: header line must contain a colon",
  "malformed_child_termination": "SIGTERM"
}
```

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Remaining proof gap:** no non-Linux platform was exercised.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** N/A — this is a new follow-up PR; no review findings exist on this head.

## Regression Test Plan

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

Sanitized exact-head AWS Crabbox run `run_55379c4d977b` passed all 18 focused tests. Exact-head real behavior run `run_f805f238ea53` passed the canonical third-party-server and malformed-subprocess scenarios above.

## Risk / Compatibility

Medium compatibility/availability risk at a narrow protocol boundary. Standards-compliant positive safe `Content-Length` frames at or below 64 MiB are unchanged. Invalid values, duplicate fields, headers above 8 KiB, bodies above 64 MiB, and invalid JSON bodies now terminate only the affected bundled LSP session instead of being accepted or left pending.

## What was not changed

- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: no outbound or public contract changes.
- Channel/provider/session/security behavior outside the fixed path: no changes.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, lockfiles: none in the three-dot PR diff.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** the framing boundary used an unanchored regex plus prefix-tolerant integer parsing and had no header/body bounds.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** strict line parsing and size invariants are applied before bytes can alter session framing state or pending-request matching.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — failing reproduction, exact-head focused GREEN, and exact-head real-server/malformed-subprocess proof all bind commit `5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3`.
- **Patch quality notes:** the change reuses existing session failure and process cleanup paths; it adds no new mutable drain/session mode and no unrelated refactor.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** the guard is located in the canonical bundled LSP stdout parser, not in downstream hover/definition tools or generic timeout handling.

target.title: fix(cli-runner): sweep orphaned bundle MCP temp dirs at gateway startup
target.body:
Fixes #105641

## What Problem This Solves

Per-run bundled MCP temp configs (`os.tmpdir()/openclaw-cli-mcp-*/mcp.json`, containing the rendered loopback URL and resolved tokens) are only reclaimed by the in-memory `cleanup()` callback returned from `prepareModeSpecificBundleMcpConfig`. When the gateway process exits with runs in flight (restart, crash, SIGKILL), the callback dies with it and the directory leaks — credential-bearing files outlive the gateway generation that issued them, and restart-heavy deployments accumulate leaked dirs until reboot. 26 leaked dirs built up over 33 days on our production host, dates correlating 1:1 with restart activity (full field data in #105641).

## Approach

A gateway-startup post-ready sidecar (`sidecars.bundle-mcp-temp-sweep`, mirroring `sidecars.session-locks`) that removes orphaned dirs. Orphan detection is **liveness-based, not age-based**:

- Live CLI children carry the config path in their argv (`--mcp-config <dir>/mcp.json`, from `injectClaudeMcpConfigArgs`), so a dir is only removed when **no visible process references it**. Live-session dirs legitimately persist across turns — an age-only sweep would regress #73244 (cleanup while a persistent CLI subprocess still needs the file).
- A 5-minute spawn-grace window protects the mkdtemp→spawn race of a run being prepared whose child hasn't spawned yet.
- The sweep **fails closed**: if the process scan yields nothing (restricted environment), everything is kept — keeping a leaked dir beats breaking a live run.
- Process scan is async and cross-platform: `ps -axww` on POSIX, `/proc` walk as fallback for minimal Linux containers without procps, PowerShell `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` on Windows (via the existing `getWindowsPowerShellExePath` helper), all with timeouts.
- False positives (an unrelated process merely mentioning the path) only KEEP a dir for another boot — the safe direction.

`BUNDLE_MCP_TEMP_PREFIX` is now a shared const so the creator (`bundle-mcp.ts`) and the sweeper cannot drift.

## Evidence

**Live reproduction of the leak on a production gateway (OpenClaw v2026.6.11, Ubuntu VPS), before this fix** — run in flight + `systemctl restart`:

```
novo temp dir: /tmp/openclaw-cli-mcp-V6tUnQ
>>> systemctl restart com run em voo...
✅ LEAK REPRODUZIDO: /tmp/openclaw-cli-mcp-V6tUnQ sobreviveu ao restart do gateway
total 4
drwx------   2 root root   60 Jul 12 14:51 .
-rw-r--r--   1 root root 1470 Jul 12 14:51 mcp.json
=== total dirs: 26
```

**Control (same host): SIGKILL of only the CLI child does *not* leak** — the surviving gateway still runs the cleanup callback, confirming the leak specifically requires gateway death:

```
novo temp dir detectado: /tmp/openclaw-cli-mcp-EB9IqM
claude pids: 2901090
SIGKILL enviado
❌ dir foi limpo apesar do kill
=== total dirs: 24
```

**Focused tests** (new `bundle-mcp-sweep.test.ts` + touched `server-startup-post-attach.test.ts`):

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
```

**Lint**: `pnpm lint` exits 0 on the branch.

**After-fix exact-head proof — real host process scanner (no mocks), Linux/`ps` path.** Ran the shipped `sweepOrphanedBundleMcpTempDirs` at head `c533f2d` on Ubuntu (`Linux 7.0.0`, Node 22.22.2, procps-ng 4.0.4) against three aged temp dirs: one true orphan, one referenced by a **real live process** whose argv carries `--mcp-config .../LIVE1/mcp.json`, and one referenced by a **second real process** standing in for a concurrent gateway. No `listCommandLines` override — the sweep used the actual host scanner:

```
=== BEFORE (3 dirs, mtime -2h):
openclaw-cli-mcp-CONC1
openclaw-cli-mcp-LIVE1
openclaw-cli-mcp-ORPHAN1
=== real processes holding LIVE1/CONC1 (host `ps -axww`):
claude --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config openclaw-cli-mcp-LIVE1/mcp.json 120
claude --mcp-config openclaw-cli-mcp-CONC1/mcp.json --other 120
=== SWEEP (real process scanner, no mock):
removed: ["openclaw-cli-mcp-ORPHAN1"]
kept:    ["openclaw-cli-mcp-CONC1","openclaw-cli-mcp-LIVE1"]
=== AFTER:
openclaw-cli-mcp-CONC1
openclaw-cli-mcp-LIVE1
```

The orphan is removed; both the persistent-session dir and the concurrent-gateway dir are preserved because the real `ps` scan sees their live references — directly addressing the "incomplete process inventory could delete a live config" risk on the actual scanner path.

### Update — owner-aware reclamation (addresses the queued-config ownership finding)

The prior revision keyed reclamation on argv liveness plus a grace window. As reviewed, the bundle MCP config is rendered at prepare time (`prepare.ts`), *before* the run enters `enqueueCliRun` (`execute.ts`), so a run waiting in the serialization queue owns a config that no child argv references yet. Past the grace window, a concurrent gateway's startup sweep could delete that dir, making the queued run spawn with a missing `--mcp-config`.

Fix (`5bf9437d`): each temp dir now carries an owner marker (`.owner.json` = creating gateway pid + Linux boot id). An aged, argv-unreferenced dir is reclaimed only once its owning gateway is gone — pid dead (`process.kill(pid, 0)`), or boot id changed by a reboot. Unmarked legacy dirs keep the prior age+liveness rule so pre-existing leaks are still swept, and a marker write failure is non-fatal (falls back to legacy), so ownership can never over-protect a leak. The primary case (gateway death with runs in flight, #105641) is unchanged: the dead gateway's pid fails the liveness probe, so the orphan is still removed.

Local validation on the rebased head (`5bf9437d`): `oxlint` clean, `tsgo:core` + `tsgo:core:test` clean, `check:temp-path-guardrails` pass, `deadcode:exports` adds no new entry (the marker name is module-private), and the `bundle-mcp-sweep` + `server-startup-post-attach` + `prepare` suites pass (217 tests).

#### Real-behavior proof — owner-aware keep/remove at exact head `5bf9437d`

Ran the exported `sweepOrphanedBundleMcpTempDirs` (esbuild-bundled from the exact-head source — the real function, not a reimplementation) on a real Linux host (node v22) with its real defaults: real `ps` process scan, real `process.kill(pid, 0)` liveness, real boot id. Two temp dirs aged 24h past the grace window, neither referenced by any live argv — one owned by a live process, one by a dead process. Redacted (no tokens, endpoints, host paths, or boot id):

```
== Setup (aged 24h, no argv reference to either dir) ==
live-owner dir  owner.json: {"pid": 2937168 (LIVE), "bootId": "<redacted-boot-id>"}
dead-owner dir  owner.json: {"pid": 2937169 (DEAD), "bootId": "<redacted-boot-id>"}
process.kill(2937168,0) -> alive=true
process.kill(2937169,0) -> alive=false

== sweepOrphanedBundleMcpTempDirs (real defaults) ==
removed: [ '<tmp>/openclaw-cli-mcp-dead-owner' ]
kept:    [ '<tmp>/openclaw-cli-mcp-live-owner' ]

== Verification on disk ==
live-owner dir still present: true  (expected true  — queued run of a live gateway preserved)
dead-owner dir reclaimed:     true (expected true  — true orphan removed)

RESULT: PASS
```

The live-owner dir (a queued run's config whose gateway is still alive, no argv reference yet) is preserved; the dead-owner dir (a true orphan) is reclaimed — the exact keep/remove distinction the owner marker adds, exercised on the final-head code with the real liveness probe.

## Tests

New `bundle-mcp-sweep.test.ts` covers the scenarios called out in the issue: gateway death with runs in flight (orphan removed), a live CLI child keeping its dir (#73244 control), a concurrent gateway instance's child keeping its dir, spawn-grace window, fail-closed on empty process scan, legacy empty dirs, and non-matching entries/missing roots. Owner-aware cases added: a queued run whose owning gateway is still alive is kept, a dead-owner dir is removed, a dir whose owner boot id predates a reboot is removed even if the pid was reused, and a live-owned dir with a matching boot id is kept.

`server-startup-post-attach.test.ts` mocks the sweep module so the existing startup test doesn't touch the real tmpdir/process table; its assertions are unchanged.

target.title: fix(gateway): always enforce path containment for session transcript archive
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `archiveSessionTranscriptsDetailed` used a single `dirname(storePath)` containment root after removing the opt-in `restrictToStoreDir` flag. This dropped valid custom transcript paths (when `storePath` is undefined) and cross-agent candidate paths, breaking the existing resolver contract.

**Solution**: Replace the single-root filter with multi-root containment matching the resolver's validated candidate boundary. The archive function now accepts candidates from the store directory, sibling agent sessions directories, and the legacy global sessions directory.

**What changed**: `archiveSessionTranscriptsDetailed` now uses a `containmentRoots` array built from the same inputs as `resolveSessionTranscriptCandidates`. Each candidate is accepted if it falls under any root. 4 new regression tests cover cross-agent, no-store custom, and poisoned path scenarios. Total: 396 tests passed.

**What did NOT change**: Function signatures remain the same (callers unchanged). Existing archive behavior for normal store-path sessions is preserved. The `restrictToStoreDir` parameter is kept as a no-op for backward compatibility. No changes to the resolver (`resolveSessionTranscriptCandidates`) or path validation logic (`resolvePathWithinSessionsDir`).

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Session transcript archive containment now matches the resolver boundary, preserving custom and cross-agent paths while rejecting poisoned paths.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx tsx /tmp/archive-proof.mjs
```
L2 real behavior proof: direct function call with real filesystem state.

**After-fix evidence**:
```
=== Before ===
storePath: /tmp/archive-proof-XXXX/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json
store transcript exists: true
cross-agent transcript exists: true

=== 1. Normal store-path archive ===
Archived: [proof-sess-1.jsonl.reset...]  archived file exists: true

=== 2. Cross-agent archive ===
Archived: 2 candidates archived file exists: true

=== 3. No-store custom path archive ===
Archived: [custom-transcript.jsonl.reset...]  archived file exists: true

=== 4. Reject poisoned non-jsonl sessionFile ===
Archived (should be empty): []

=== 5. Reject poisoned with storePath ===
Archived count (expected 1, valid fallback): 1

=== All scenarios verified ===
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All five scenarios pass. Normal store-path, cross-agent, and no-store custom transcript archives produce the expected archive files. Poisoned `/etc/passwd` paths are rejected both with and without storePath.

**What was not tested**: The full gateway archive/reset/delete HTTP flow with a running gateway server. The containment logic is exercised at the function level with real filesystem state, which directly validates the changed surface.

## Tests and validation

| Suite | Files | Tests | Result |
|-------|-------|-------|--------|
| session-utils.fs | 4 | 396 | All passed |
| Archive-specific | 4 | 24 focused | All passed |
| session-transcript-key | 4 | 24 | All passed |

## Risk checklist

**Risk level**: Low — containment boundary widened to match existing resolver contract, no new edge cases introduced.
**Mitigation**: 4 regression tests covering cross-agent, custom path, and poisoned path scenarios; real behavior proof with filesystem state.
**merge-risk**: Low — widens (not narrows) accepted paths; any previously working path preserved.

- [x] This change preserves backward compatibility
- [x] This change has been tested — 396 tests pass
- [x] Regression tests added for cross-agent, no-store custom, and poisoned paths
- [x] Breaking changes documented in Summary — none

target.title: fix(nostr): keep profile imports as cancellable drafts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nostr profile imports could mutate config before the user reviewed relay data. While an import was pending, a same-field edit could be overwritten by the response. Cancel could close the form while a server-side merge still persisted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI now requests `autoMerge: false`, treats relay data as a draft, locks profile controls while importing, and aborts/invalidate imports on Cancel, disconnect, or form replacement. Late responses cannot update a hidden or newer form. Explicit **Save & Publish** remains the write path.

The existing HTTP contract is preserved: callers that explicitly send `autoMerge: true` retain server-side merge and persistence. Only the Control UI opts into draft mode.

## User Impact

Imported values fill the open form for review. Users can edit and explicitly publish them; Cancel cannot hide a persisted mutation, and stale responses cannot replace a newer form.

## Evidence

### Real Control UI + relay/browser proof

A standalone Chromium run drove the actual Control UI. Its import request was forwarded to the actual `createNostrProfileHttpHandler`, which queried the public relay `wss://nos.lol`. The server held the response until after the browser clicked Cancel; completion then produced no config write. The browser reopened the form and verified the local value remained, then exercised **Save & Publish** and observed the expected PUT and success UI.

target.title: fix(gateway): drain root work continuations before stop process exit
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks that were already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. This happens because the session is removed from the shutdown tracker synchronously before the hook fires asynchronously via `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation`, and the direct-stop path (`handleStopAfterServerClose`) exits the process without waiting for these continuations to settle. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

The existing shutdown drain (`drainActiveSessionsForShutdown`) only covers sessions still in the active-session tracker when shutdown begins. Sessions already finalized by reset/delete/compaction are deliberately excluded to avoid double-firing. Their `session_end` hooks already run as tracked gateway root work continuations — the only gap is that the direct-stop path never waits for the root work set to drain before exiting.

Instead of changing the `emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook` signature (which would alter latency on every normal finalization path), this fix adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root work set to the direct-stop path, matching the approach recommended by ClawSweeper in the issue review.

The drain uses a referenced `setTimeout` poll loop (not `.unref()`) so that the polling timer keeps the Node.js event loop alive during the wait. The 2-second timeout bound and the `exitProcess(0)` fallback in the caller guarantee that a stuck hook cannot block shutdown past the supervisor stop timeout.

#### User Impact

No visible impact under normal operation. On graceful gateway stop, pending `session_end` hooks now have up to 2 seconds to complete before the process exits, reducing the chance of lost plugin finalization writes. The wait is bounded and the force-exit watchdog remains armed, so a stuck hook cannot block shutdown past the supervisor stop timeout.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors on changed files
- **Tests:**
  ```
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts

  ✓ |unit| src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts (17 tests)
  ✓ |cli|  src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts (45 tests)

  Test Files  2 passed (2)
       Tests  62 passed (62)
  ```
  - `gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 17 tests pass (+4: `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` success / timeout / immediate zero-count / poll-and-release)
  - `run-loop.test.ts` — 45 tests pass (+2: direct-stop drains root work before exit; warns and still exits on drain timeout; +1 mock fix)
- **Change scope:** 4 files, +116 lines
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts` — new `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` helper (referenced poll, no `.unref()`)
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts` — drain call in `handleStopAfterServerClose` before `exitProcess(0)`
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 4 new tests for drain helper
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts` — 2 new regression tests + mock fix
  - Directory scope: `src/cli`, `src/process` — no config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies** — reuses existing `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount`
- **ClawSweeper P1 fix:** removed `.unref()` from the drain poll loop (`src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts:312`). The referenced `setTimeout` keeps the event loop alive during the bounded wait, so Node cannot exit naturally before the next poll fires. The 2-second timeout and caller's `exitProcess(0)` guarantee no infinite hang.
- **Live proof:** ran standalone script exercising `gateway-work-admission` internals under the exact race scenario:

```
=== Gateway Stop Root Work Drain — Proof Log ===

[Case 1] No pending root work — immediate return
  drain returned: true (0.1ms)
  ✓ returns true immediately
  ✓ <10ms (no busy-wait)

[Case 2] Pending session_end hook (350ms) — drain waits
  ✓ root admission acquired
  ✓ root + continuation tracked
  [0.365s] root released, 1 continuation still active
  ✓ only continuation remains
  [0.365s] SIGTERM received → starting stop drain...
  [0.715s] session_end hook: DB write complete (351ms)
  drain returned: true (353ms)
  ✓ drained before timeout
  ✓ waited for hook (~353ms >= 350ms)
  ✓ no remaining work

[Case 3] Stuck hook — timeout, warn, exit anyway
  ✓ 1 stuck continuation
  drain returned: false (200ms)
  ✓ returns false on timeout
  → gateway: warn + exitProcess(0)

[Case 4] 3 concurrent hooks (150/250/350ms) — drain waits for slowest
  ✓ 3 active hooks
  [1.071s] hook #1 done (151ms)
  [1.172s] hook #2 done (251ms)
  [1.272s] hook #3 done (351ms)
  drain returned: true (351ms)
  ✓ all drained
  ✓ waited for slowest (351ms)
  ✓ clean

=== Results: 14 passed / 0 failed ===
```

- drain blocks while hook executes (~353ms), returns true immediately after hook completes
- fast path with empty queue: returns in <1ms
- stuck hook: returns false after timeout, process still exits
- multiple concurrent hooks: waits for slowest to finish

This PR is AI-assisted. I have personally verified all code and AI was used for syntax.

## Summary

Fix two ClickClack outbound failure modes:

1. Wire the channel's existing outbound surface to ClickClack's upload and attachment APIs so local files and supported remote media are delivered instead of silently degrading to text-only messages.
2. Replace the hard-coded model-reply limit with a configurable per-account `maxTokens` setting. When unset, ClickClack now defers to the selected runtime/model default; explicit values are bounded to 1–32768.

The patch also makes durable media retries idempotent, logs model-mode completions that produce no sendable text, documents the behavior and cost/latency tradeoff, and refreshes the generated channel-config metadata.

## What Problem This Solves

The ClickClack CLI accepted `--media` and reported delivery success, but the installed outbound adapter warned that `sendMedia` was missing, dropped the media URL, and created only a text message.

Separately, `replyMode: "model"` always called `llm.complete` with `maxTokens: 96`. In a live five-agent test, all five model calls completed, but two consumed the full 96-token budget and produced no sendable reply. Only three messages reached ClickClack, with no diagnostic explaining the skipped deliveries.

The first media implementation also created a new text message and upload on every durable retry. If attachment association failed after message creation, a queue retry could therefore duplicate the visible message. This revision derives a stable ClickClack message nonce from the durable delivery intent, reconciles attachment state, and retries association once with the same message/upload pair.

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Skills / tool execution

- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- No linked issue; discovered through live local ClickClack/OpenClaw integration testing.
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Evidence

- Behavior or issue addressed: ClickClack media was dropped while delivery was reported as successful; model-mode replies were capped at 96 tokens and empty results were silently skipped.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node v24.14.1, local ClickClack server at `127.0.0.1:18082`, five named ClickClack bot accounts.
- Before media evidence:

```text
media URLs will be dropped and text fallback will be used
```

- Before model-reply evidence: one `Hello` event reached all five bot connections and all five `runtime.llm` calls completed. ClickClack persisted replies from Mustang, Clipper, and Nighthawk only. Blackbird and Dragon Lady both reached the hard-coded 96-token ceiling and emitted no outbound message request.
- Exact live media verification after this patch:

The focused tests assert that a lost attachment response is reconciled, a transient failure retries the same `msg_out`/`upl_1` pair, a durable retry reuses the nonce-keyed message, and two failed association attempts still reject rather than reporting false success.

The final unset-account regression used the patched plugin with `maxTokens`

## Root Cause

- Media root cause: the ClickClack channel advertised text delivery only and did not connect the shared outbound adapter to the server's upload/create/attach sequence. Core therefore dropped `mediaUrl` and used its text fallback.
- Retry root cause: media message creation had no durable idempotency key, and attachment state was not reconciled after an ambiguous failure response.
- Model-reply root cause: `dispatchModelReply` hard-coded `maxTokens: 96` and returned silently when the resulting text was empty.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no live media-delivery test verified that an attachment was persisted and retrievable, no regression covered ambiguous attachment failures, and no warning identified empty model-mode completions.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- ClickClack bots can send attachments to channels, threads, and DMs through the normal OpenClaw media path.
- Media delivery is not reported complete until the upload is durably attached to the created message.
- Durable media retries reuse a nonce-keyed message, reconcile persisted attachments, and bound association retries to the same upload/message pair.
- Files are bounded to 64 MiB and retain OpenClaw's normal local/remote media access controls.
- `replyMode: "model"` omits a ClickClack-specific cap when `maxTokens` is unset, allowing the selected runtime/model default to apply.
- Each account can set `maxTokens` from 1 to 32768.
- Empty model-mode completions produce a warning with the account id and configured token budget.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`): Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`): Yes — optional `channels.clickclack.maxTokens` and per-account `maxTokens`
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`): No

target.title: feat(discord): show subagent progress
target.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in Discord-scoped sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message, including count reactions, durable failure marker behavior, and typing keepalive while tracked work is active.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord users currently have little visible feedback when an assistant turn delegates work to tracked sub-agents. Long-running turns can look idle after the initial message even though background sub-agents are still running, and a sub-agent failure is not visible on the original Discord message.

Discord also cannot represent concurrent work by adding the same emoji reaction multiple times from the same bot/user, so progress needs a count-based reaction model instead of repeated identical reactions.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Discord users get immediate, lightweight progress feedback during delegated work without waiting for the final assistant reply:

- `1️⃣`, `2️⃣`, etc. show the current active tracked sub-agent count for the turn
- the count reaction is replaced as the active count changes
- the count reaction disappears when no tracked sub-agents remain active
- `🔴` remains if any tracked sub-agent ends with a non-OK outcome
- typing stays active while tracked sub-agents are still running

Operators can configure the behavior with `channels.discord.subagentProgress`, including reaction progress, count emoji, failure emoji, typing keepalive, interval, and max-duration TTL.

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

## Linked Context

No linked issues or external context were listed in the current PR body.

## What Changes

This PR adds Discord-scoped, best-effort sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message. The feature is opt-in with `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`.

When enabled:

- one configurable count reaction shows the number of currently active tracked sub-agents (`1️⃣` … `🔟` by default)
- count changes replace the previous count reaction instead of accumulating multiple ordinal reactions
- zero active tracked sub-agents removes the count reaction
- any non-OK completion leaves a durable configurable failure marker (`🔴` by default)
- Discord typing is kept alive independently while tracked sub-agents remain active, then stops when all tracked work finishes or the safety TTL expires

The implementation threads the source Discord message id through native `sessions_spawn`, tracked ACP spawn, requester origin metadata, and internal Discord progress hook handling so the Discord extension can target the correct parent message. Non-Discord callers and callers without a source message id keep existing behavior.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds source/current message id propagation through delivery context and `sessions_spawn` tool context.
- Carries that id into native sub-agent spawn and tracked ACP registration.
- Keeps public plugin hook/requester metadata narrow while the Discord extension uses an internal Discord-only event shape for source-message progress targeting.
- Emits progress cleanup at run completion even when ordinary `subagent_ended` delivery is deferred.
- Adds a Discord progress tracker keyed by account id, parent channel id, typing/thread target id, and source message id to avoid thread collisions.
- Tracks active run ids and derives the displayed count from current active set size.
- Replaces the displayed count reaction when the active count changes, removes it at zero, and caps counts above the configured emoji list to the final configured emoji.
- Uses `unref` on typing timers where supported so keepalive intervals do not keep Node alive.
- Updates Discord config schema, exported config types, UI hints, generated channel config metadata, and docs.

## Tests / Verification

Focused validation and static/config/docs gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `20a11bf331429ed2fd521636910b4aa07c5dcc24`
- Current PR head: `0f0ea76085d4ddc271aa25bab129f9c518f95992`
- Re-squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.
- Removed invalid/unnecessary delivered-text visibility experiment from `d17f593b4d4428f6ba7318f55eb40d76c3932094`; legitimate Discord sub-agent progress behavior remains.

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live Discord proof for source-message progress behavior, not only tests. The requested coverage was: count reaction add/replace/remove behavior, normal channel context, thread/forum context, concurrent tracked sub-agents, typing keepalive while tracked work is active, typing stop/drain and TTL behavior, and durable failure-marker behavior after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle.

The live proof below covers those requested behaviors: normal channel success, thread-bound success, concurrent count replacement/increment/decrement/clear, typing keepalive/stop plus TTL guard logs, and a durable failure marker retained on the original source message after non-OK lifecycle. Private host/path/token/session/network values are redacted; Discord IDs/timestamps shown are included only where they are needed to tie the proof to the source-message behavior.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

Live Discord API proof was run from the installed PR stack on Dev-01 using `OpenClaw 2026.6.10-beta.1` at local HEAD `f15c88bd6f9 stack: combine beta memory slots and Discord progress`, with:

- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.reactions.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.typing.enabled=true`

Observed live behavior in Discord:

- **Normal channel success:** a Discord-originated parent turn spawned a tracked sub-agent run (`8c6dbfa0-e021-4c3a-9992-328de22caa13`). The source Discord message showed the active count reaction while the child was running, typing stayed active during child work, and the count reaction was removed after the child completed. Child proof line: `NORMAL_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:48:33Z`.
- **Thread-bound success:** a thread-bound Discord sub-agent run (`01fa6443-4fc1-409d-9cf3-969ce433edbd`) completed successfully while progress was shown from the Discord parent context. Child proof line: `THREAD_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:49:50Z`.
- **Concurrent count replacement:** two overlapping tracked sub-agent runs (`4b2701ef-85b0-41d5-a87f-f72924e21869` and `9a5b1e70-5b3b-4820-bb5f-cb6cb7b2a926`) exercised count add/replace/remove behavior. The Discord source message count reaction incremented while both children were active, decremented as the first child completed, and cleared after the second child completed. Child proof lines: `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_2_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:23Z` and `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_3_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:36Z`.
- **Typing keepalive/stop:** Discord typing was visible while tracked sub-agents were active and stopped after tracked work drained. Earlier long-running proof passes also hit the configured typing safety TTL, with gateway logs showing `[typing] TTL exceeded (60000ms), auto-stopping typing indicator`, confirming the timeout guard executes.

Additional observation: after the final child drains, there can be a brief visual gap before the parent posts its final reconciliation response. That appears to be parent-yield lifecycle behavior rather than this PR's sub-agent progress tracker; it is being tracked separately as a follow-up investigation and is not treated as a blocker for this PR.

Additional durable failure-marker proof was captured from a real Discord source message after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle:

- **Failure marker:** source message `1518528276031602788` in Discord channel `1507934992699756645` retained the configured durable failure reaction `🔴` with count `1` and `me: true` after the non-OK sub-agent lifecycle. The source message timestamp was `2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z`. A later follow-up heartbeat at `2026-06-22T08:29:48.355Z` reported a separate verification pass, confirming the red marker was left on the original source message rather than being ordinary final text delivery.

Redacted observation:

```json
{
  "channel_id": "1507934992699756645",
  "message_id": "1518528276031602788",
  "timestampUtc": "2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z",
  "content": "Extensively check over the branch end-to-end against the recommended fix and prior investigation/research to ensure everything is clean, finalized, and polished.",
  "reactions": [
    {
      "emoji": { "name": "🔴" },
      "count": 1,
      "me": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## Compatibility and Risk

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

## PR/Commit Surface Breakdown

Source: 29 files, +846 / -81
Tests: 11 files, +1232 / -20
Total: 40 files, +2078 / -101

## Reviewer Checklist

- Confirm Discord progress remains opt-in and best-effort.
- Review source-message id propagation and tracker keying for channel/thread isolation.
- Confirm live Discord proof and focused tests cover add/replace/remove reactions, failure marker, typing, and config behavior.

---
Maintenance update: squashed to `381aa6f701d588adc4f18fd9dffcb84d6b41b953` after test-surface optimization only; behavior coverage and focused validation were preserved.

---

### Rebase/conflict resolution proof (2026-06-26)
- Rebased independently onto upstream `openclaw/openclaw` main `dd0e4f6e61b808fb77a5b85d2773e73c0dee2078`.
- Old head: `381aa6f701d588adc4f18fd9dffcb84d6b41b953`; new head: `265ab6294af01007c10d3c2406fc2494deec41be`.
- Resolved upstream/base conflict in `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` by preserving this PR's Discord subagent progress SDK surface changes and updating the current upstream public SDK budgets.
- Validation: `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`; `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check`; focused Vitest run covering Discord subagent hooks/config schema, agent spawn hooks/tooling, subagent registry completion/lifecycle/store/core tests, plugin boundary invariants, and delivery context tests.

target.title: fix(gateway): add base64 validation before decode in persistInboundImagesForTranscript
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #105837

**Problem**: `persistInboundImagesForTranscript` decodes base64 image data via `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` without validating the encoding first. Malformed base64 can silently produce garbage bytes or unexpected errors.

**Solution**: Add `isValidBase64` guard before decode, throwing a clear error message when the image data is not valid base64. Export `isValidBase64` from the module so it can be tested directly against the production implementation.

**What changed**: One guard in `src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts:74` — `if (!isValidBase64(image.data))` before `Buffer.from` decode. Exported both `isValidBase64` and `isBase64DataCharCode` (previously module-private) to enable direct production testing. Rewrote `chat-attachments.base64.test.ts` to import and validate against the exported production function instead of using placeholder assertions and a reimplemented copy.

**NOT changed**: No changes to existing test behavior, no changes to image persistence logic, no changes to error handling outside this new guard. All existing tests continue to pass. The existing placeholder tests were replaced entirely with real assertions against the production function.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `isValidBase64` guard validates base64 before `Buffer.from` decode in `persistInboundImagesForTranscript`.
**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw `main@HEAD` with this patch applied.
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `pnpm test src/gateway/chat-attachments.base64.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
**After-fix evidence**: 24 tests passed across 4 Vitest shards (see terminal output in Tests section below).
**Observed result after the fix**: Valid base64 accepted (`dGVzdA==` → true), empty string rejected (false), invalid chars rejected (false), unpadded base64 rejected (false), padding-in-middle rejected (false), excessive padding rejected (false).
**What was not tested**: End-to-end Gateway server with actual image uploads (requires full runtime setup); the guard is unit-testable at the function level and further validated by existing `chat-attachments.test.ts` integration path.

## Tests and validation

```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/chat-attachments.base64.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ isValidBase64 — production function > accepts valid padded base64
 ✓ isValidBase64 — production function > rejects empty string
 ✓ isValidBase64 — production function > rejects string with invalid characters
 ✓ isValidBase64 — production function > rejects unpadded base64 (length not divisible by 4)
 ✓ isValidBase64 — production function > rejects strings with padding in middle
 ✓ isValidBase64 — production function > rejects strings with too much padding

 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
```

Validated against the exported production `isValidBase64` function:

| Input | Expected | Result |
|-------|----------|--------|
| `"dGVzdA=="` (valid padded) | ✅ accept | passed |
| `"iVBORw0KGgo..."` (valid PNG base64) | ✅ accept | passed |
| `""` (empty) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"invalid!"` (invalid chars) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"abc"` (unpadded, length 3) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"abc=defg"` (padding in middle) | ❌ reject | passed |
| `"a==="` (excessive padding) | ❌ reject | passed |

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — valid base64 inputs continue to decode as before
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

---

target.body:
## Summary

- Routes the live Microsoft Teams `signin.token-exchange` and `signin.verify-state` routes through OpenClaw's bounded SSO User Token helper instead of the Teams SDK's unbounded axios `res.data` path.
- Keeps the existing sender-policy gate and preserves token persistence for both `activity.from.id` and `activity.from.aadObjectId` aliases.
- Preserves the SDK cloud-specific Bot Framework User Token service URL, so USGov/USGovDoD/China SSO routes keep using the same token host as the SDK route they replace.
- Keeps the 16 MiB successful-response cap and existing non-OK error handling for Bot Framework User Token service calls.
- Adds production-route tests proving normal, oversized, and non-public-cloud User Token responses through the registered sign-in routes.

## Linked context

No linked issue; this is a narrow follow-up to the bounded-response-read hardening series for Microsoft Teams SSO.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: The previous PR version bounded only the direct SSO helper path. The production monitor-registered `signin.token-exchange` and `signin.verify-state` routes still delegated to the Teams SDK handlers, whose User Token client reads axios `res.data` without a response-size cap. This update moves those live routes onto OpenClaw's bounded helper while preserving the SDK cloud token-service URL via `app.cloud.tokenServiceUrl`.

Real environment tested: Linux x86-64, Node 22.22.0, local OpenClaw worktree with installed repo dependencies, real Node/Web `Response` streams, and the msteams extension test runtime.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
