target.title: fix(approval): distinguish policy vs non-persistable reason when Allow Always unavailable
target.body:
Fixes #97069.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running commands with shell redirection (e.g. `openclaw --version 2>&1`) would see "The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable" — even when their effective policy is `ask=on-miss`. All nine approval prompt renderers (reply, forwarder, agent-facing, Control UI, reaction, embedded handler, Telegram handler, Telegram forwarding, and gateway API) blamed the policy instead of the real cause: the command is non-persistable and cannot be saved as an allow-always rule.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveExecApprovalAllowedDecisions()` returns the same `["allow-once", "deny"]` for both `ask=always` (policy) and one-shot persistence (non-persistable command). Downstream renderers had no way to distinguish the two cases.

Rather than introducing a new typed protocol field (which previous attempts attempted across 65+ files), we thread the existing `ask` field — already present in the request payload, approval view, and gateway pipeline — through the approval-pending data pipeline so renderers can branch on it. Approval policy logic is unchanged.

The `node` host path uses `approvalDecisionAsk` (`maxAsk(hostAsk, nodeAsk)`) to keep the reasoning consistent with `allowedDecisions` computation even when the node policy is stricter than the host policy.

## User Impact

Users with `ask=on-miss` (or any non-always policy) who run commands with shell redirection will now see:

> Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).

Instead of the misleading policy message. Users with `ask=always` see the same policy message as before. The Control UI shows a distinct non-persistable warning using a new i18n key (`allowAlwaysNonPersistable`).

| `ask` input | Message shown |
|---|---|
| `"always"` | "The effective approval policy requires approval every time…" |
| `"on-miss"` (one-shot) | "Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted…" |
| `"off"` (shell redirect) | "Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted…" |
| absent / null | "The effective approval policy requires approval every time…" (safe default) |

## Evidence

**18 files, +109/−23 lines.** Core logic is 52 lines; tests add 57 lines.

**Renderers fixed (all 9):** reply, forwarder, agent-facing, Control UI, reaction, embedded handler, Telegram handler, Telegram forwarding, gateway API error message.

**Tests added/updated:** 5 test files — new non-persistable test cases in reply, forwarder, reaction, and Control UI tests; updated assertions in server-methods tests.

**CI:** `tsgo:core` zero type errors; `ui:i18n:check` passes (20 locales clean with 1 English fallback each for the new key).

target.title: fix(agents): decouple MCP retirement from browser cleanup
target.body:
Related: #76233
Related: #101830

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a completed run-mode subagent waits for sequential browser-tab cleanup before retiring its bundle MCP runtime and starting completion delivery. A browser close request can wait up to the browser service timeout per tab, so one run with several tabs can delay MCP retirement, the completion announcement, and the next same-session turn.

The concrete sequential browser-cleanup delay is separate from the MCP lease-disposal race covered by #76233 and the related #101830 work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser cleanup is dispatched as independent owner-scoped work, while MCP retirement and completion announcement proceed after the existing generation and lease-safety checks. Browser operations hold a per-session access gate for their full request; cleanup takes the exclusive gate, so a successor browser turn waits safely instead of racing an already-issued close request.

The browser registry tracks the opaque run owner and an ordered ownership claim. Successor reuse transfers ownership; late predecessor callbacks cannot reclaim or remove the successor tab. Failed non-ignorable closes remain tracked for a later cleanup, and legacy unowned tabs remain eligible for cleanup.

`runId` remains an additive, optional Plugin SDK context field. It is host-issued, stable for the active run, opaque, and absent outside an active run. Plugins may use it only to key ephemeral plugin-owned resources and cleanup; they must not parse it, persist it as application data, expose it to users, or use it as an authentication or authorization boundary. The contract is documented in `docs/plugins/building-plugins.md` and covered at the `defineToolPlugin` factory boundary in `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts`; the existing agent-context test covers runtime propagation.

## User Impact

Run-mode subagent completion no longer waits for the browser service to close every tracked tab before MCP retirement and completion delivery begin. A successor turn can start its non-browser work immediately and its browser work is admitted after the old cleanup gate releases, preserving tab safety. App-view MCP leases continue to defer retirement until their release path completes.

target.title: fix(gateway): count pending restarts toward maxRestartsPerHour budget
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves
close #105189
When a channel is permanently stuck in a pending restart state, two issues arise:

1. **Budget bypass**: The health monitor skips the maxRestartsPerHour check for pending restarts, causing infinite restart attempts.
2. **No completion pass**: Even after counting pending restarts toward the hourly budget, a recovery that consumed the last slot cannot finish — it hits the cap on the next tick.
3. **Rollover starvation**: After the completion pass is exhausted, old restart records eventually fall out of the 1-hour window — but `completionPassAllowed` stays `true`, silently starving the channel forever.

### Why This Change Was Made

Issue 1: The `continuingPendingRestart` guard prevented both the rate-limit check and the restart record update for pending restarts. Once a channel entered a permanently-pending state, every monitor tick would attempt another restart without counting it against the hourly budget.

Issue 2: With the cap applied uniformly, a pending recovery that used the last hourly slot would be blocked on the very next check, preventing it from ever completing.

Issue 3 (rollover): `completionPassAllowed` is set to `true` once the completion pass is granted, and only reset when a new restart record is pushed. After the hourly window rolls over and old records are pruned, the flag remains `true`, so the channel is stuck with zero budget — even though capacity has reopened.

### What Changed

- Pending restarts count toward `maxRestartsPerHour` — the rate limit guard no longer skips for pending restarts
- Pending restarts are recorded in `restartsThisHour` — the record update no longer skips for pending restarts
- **One completion pass**: When a pending recovery hits the hourly cap, it gets one extra pass to finish, without pushing a new restart record. A `completionPassAllowed` flag tracks this — reset on each new restart record
- **Rollover reset**: `pruneOldRestarts` now resets `completionPassAllowed` when pruning old entries reopens budget capacity (`before >= maxRestarts && after < maxRestarts`)
- The cooldown check (fresh-restart throttle) still correctly skips for pending restarts, since they continue an already-begun recovery

### Does one pending completion attempt exceed the configured recorded maximum?

**Yes, by 1.** The `maxRestartsPerHour` config limits *recorded restart slots* in the rolling window. A continuing pending restart that consumes the last slot gets one extra recovery attempt (a *completion pass*) without recording a new slot. In practice this means:

- Normal channels: capped at exactly `maxRestartsPerHour` restarts per hour (all recorded)
- Stuck pending channels: capped at `maxRestartsPerHour + 1` calls per hour (the extra call is the unrecorded completion pass)
- After the hourly window rolls over and old records are pruned, `completionPassAllowed` resets, allowing the same pattern in the fresh window

This is intentional: the completion pass prevents a stuck pending channel from being permanently starved after consuming its last budget slot, while still preventing infinite restart loops. The completion pass does not count toward the recorded restart history, so it does not extend the window.

### Evidence

#### Regression Tests

`src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts:569` — caps pending recovery restarts at the configured maxRestartsPerHour with one completion pass: Simulates a channel where every restart transitions to pending, configures maxRestartsPerHour=2, runs 30 seconds of health checks, and asserts startChannel is called exactly 3 times (2 budgeted + 1 completion pass).

`src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts:607` — grants one completion pass for a pending recovery that consumed the last hourly slot: Tick-by-tick verification proving the completion pass is exactly one.

`src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts:945` — resets completion-pass flag when pruning reopens hourly budget: Exhausts budget (3 calls), confirms capped, then advances time just past the 1-hour prune point. Proves the first post-rollover pending attempt consumes a fresh budget slot (call 4 → 5 → 6 with completion pass), then caps again.

`src/gateway/live-rollover.test.ts` — continuous, timestamped, redacted gateway log capture covering the full lifecycle across one hourly rollover boundary (see output below).

#### Test Output

```
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  188 passed (188)
```

#### Live Gateway Logs — Scenario 1: Normal pending recovery completes

```
[health-monitor] started
[health-monitor] [whatsapp:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: disconnected)
[health-monitor] [whatsapp:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)
```
→ 2 calls. Channel recovered. Budget (5) not exhausted.

#### Live Gateway Logs — Scenario 2: Permanent pending retries cap correctly

```
[health-monitor] started
[health-monitor] [discord:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: disconnected)    ← slot 1/2
[health-monitor] [discord:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)         ← slot 2/2
[health-monitor] [discord:default] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)         ← completion pass
[health-monitor] [discord:default] health-monitor: hit 2 restarts/hour limit, skipping  ← capped
  ... (repeated 4×)
```

#### Live Gateway Logs — Scenario 3: Continuous rollover lifecycle (full hour)

Continuous, timestamped, redacted test output covering the capped state → 1-hour rollover → renewed attempts → completion pass → second cap:

```
[health-monitor] started (interval: 0s, startup-grace: 0s, channel-connect-grace: 120s)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: restarting (reason: disconnected)   ← call #1 (initial)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)        ← call #2 (slot 2/2)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)        ← call #3 (completion pass)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: hit 2 restarts/hour limit, skipping ← CAP #1
  ... ~35,940 skipped (capped) across 1-hour window ...

  *** ~1 hour passes — pruneOldRestarts reopens budget ***

[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)        ← call #4 (rollover, budget reopened)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)        ← call #5 (slot 2/2 in new window)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stopped)        ← call #6 (completion pass in new window)
[health-monitor] [dummy:main] health-monitor: hit 2 restarts/hour limit, skipping ← CAP #2 (after rollover)
  ... ~35,940 skipped (capped) ...
```

**Lifecycle**: calls 1–3 exhaust the first hourly budget (2 slots + 1 completion pass), then ~35,940 health checks skip while capped. After `pruneOldRestarts` removes records older than 1 hour, the budget reopens: calls 4–6 repeat the same pattern (2 slots + 1 completion pass) in the fresh 1-hour window. After call 6, the second cap activates — the channel is again rate-limited.

target.title: fix(github-copilot): reject unsupported OAuth enterprise domain before refresh and model routing
target.body:
## Summary
A legacy `github-copilot` OAuth profile can carry an `enterpriseUrl` that is not a GitHub Copilot host. Current `main` templates that persisted value straight into the endpoint it sends the bearer credential to. The refresh path sends the refresh token to `api.<persisted-domain>`, and the model-routing path derives the completions base URL from the same credential, so an unexpired credential keeps routing its access token to that origin without ever reaching a refresh. No allowlist is applied on either path.

This rejects an off-allowlist persisted origin before a request is issued and before a model URL is produced.

## Root cause
`src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts`. Two egress points, both reachable from persisted state.

Refresh, before:

```ts
export async function refreshGitHubCopilotToken(refreshToken: string, enterpriseDomain?: string) {
  const domain = enterpriseDomain || "github.com";
  const urls = getUrls(domain);
  const raw = await fetchJson(urls.copilotTokenUrl, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${refreshToken}`, ...COPILOT_HEADERS },
  });
```

Model routing, before:

```ts
modifyModels(models: Model[], credentials: OAuthCredentials): Model[] {
  const creds = credentials as CopilotCredentials;
  const domain = creds.enterpriseUrl ? (normalizeDomain(creds.enterpriseUrl) ?? undefined) : undefined;
  const baseUrl = getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl(creds.access, domain);
  return models.map((m) => (m.provider === "github-copilot" ? { ...m, baseUrl } : m));
}
```

`normalizeDomain` only parses a hostname, it does not check one. `refreshToken` and `modifyModels` are both live on current `main`: `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts` registers `githubCopilotOAuthProvider` in the built-in OAuth registry, `oauth/index.ts:107` calls `provider.refreshToken(creds)`, and `src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:392-395` calls `oauthProvider.modifyModels(combined, cred)` for every `oauth` credential.

## Fix
An off-allowlist origin means the stored access token may itself have been minted by that origin, so its `proxy-ep` is not trustworthy either. The credential is therefore refused as a whole rather than coerced onto `github.com`, which would present an enterprise-scoped token to the wrong GitHub origin.

```ts
export function getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl(token?: string, enterpriseDomain?: string): string {
  if (enterpriseDomain && !isSupportedGithubCopilotDomain(enterpriseDomain)) {
    throw new Error(`Refusing to route GitHub Copilot requests for unsupported enterprise domain "${enterpriseDomain}". ...`);
  }
  ...
}

modifyModels(models: Model[], credentials: OAuthCredentials): Model[] {
  const creds = credentials as CopilotCredentials;
  if (!isSupportedGithubCopilotDomain(creds.enterpriseUrl)) {
    return models.filter((m) => m.provider !== "github-copilot");
  }
  const baseUrl = getGitHubCopilotBaseUrl(creds.access, creds.enterpriseUrl);
  return models.map((m) => (m.provider === "github-copilot" ? { ...m, baseUrl } : m));
}
```

`modifyModels` withholds the models rather than throwing, because it runs inside the model-registry loop for every provider and a throw there would break the whole model list. Withholding leaves the access token with no route. `refreshGitHubCopilotToken` rejects before issuing a request, `loginGitHubCopilot` rejects an unsupported host up front, and `formatAuthDoctorHint` points affected users at re-authentication, mirroring the existing qwen-portal hint.

## Why this is the right boundary
Every path that turns a persisted or user-supplied domain into a bearer-bearing URL now validates first: login, refresh, and model routing. Supported hosts are unchanged, `github.com` and `*.ghe.com` data-residency tenants still route and refresh exactly as before, so the compatibility cost falls only on credentials whose origin was never a Copilot host.

Rebased onto current `main`, which moved GitHub Copilot into `extensions/github-copilot`. That plugin owns a `token`-type profile and is a different credential shape; it already resolves its host through the SDK allowlist. The legacy `oauth`-type profile path fixed here is still registered and executable on `main` (the proof below resolves it through the real registry), so this is not obsolete code and the plugin does not already cover it. The allowlist and the new `isSupportedGithubCopilotDomain` predicate move to a dependency-free `plugin-sdk` leaf so the core OAuth runtime can share them without closing a module cycle; `plugin-sdk/provider-auth` re-exports `normalizeGithubCopilotDomain`, so `extensions/github-copilot/domain.ts` keeps its existing import unchanged.

A token's `proxy-ep` is still trusted when the minting origin is on the allowlist, which matches the plugin's own `deriveCopilotApiBaseUrlFromToken`. That trust is exactly what this patch withdraws when the origin is not on the allowlist.

## Verification
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles.doctor.test.ts` passes, 31 tests. The 5 new domain and model-routing cases fail on pristine `main` (`copilot-api`/`api.attacker.example` produced, refresh resolves) and pass with the patch.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/github-copilot` is unchanged by this patch: 13 failed / 109 passed both on pristine `main` and with the patch, all in `extensions/github-copilot/index.test.ts` and unrelated to these files.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `oxfmt --check` clean on all 6 changed files.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` clean; `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` reports no error in any changed file (pre-existing errors in `ui/src/components/mcp-app-view.ts` only).
- Full `pnpm build` not run.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a persisted github-copilot OAuth profile whose `enterpriseUrl` is not a Copilot host sends its bearer refresh token to that origin on refresh, and routes its access token to that origin during model use even when it never refreshes.
Real environment tested: the real built-in OAuth provider registry on pristine main afb282ee68 and on the patched tree at b85bd5db1f, resolved through `getOAuthProvider("github-copilot")` exactly as `oauth/index.ts` and `model-registry.ts` do, then driving the real `modifyModels` and `refreshToken` of `githubCopilotOAuthProvider`. The persisted credential, the registry, the provider, the allowlist and the doctor hint are all real; the only thing replaced is the outbound network boundary, a recording `fetch` that captures the URL and Authorization header instead of sending the credential to a real host. Scenarios B and C are unchanged controls.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: resolve `getOAuthProvider("github-copilot")` from the real registry, then for each persisted credential call `provider.modifyModels([gpt-5@github-copilot, claude-sonnet-5@anthropic], credential)` and `await provider.refreshToken(credential)`, recording every outbound request.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main afb282ee68)
registry lookup getOAuthProvider("github-copilot") -> GitHub Copilot

A. legacy profile minted by an off-allowlist host
  persisted enterpriseUrl: attacker.example
  model routing:  gpt-5 -> https://api.attacker.example
  token refresh:  completed
  requests carrying the credential: 1
    -> https://api.attacker.example/copilot_internal/v2/token   Bearer gho_VICTIM_REFRESH_TOKEN

B. data-residency tenant (control)
  persisted enterpriseUrl: acme.ghe.com
  model routing:  gpt-5 -> https://api.acme.ghe.com
  token refresh:  completed
  requests carrying the credential: 1
    -> https://api.acme.ghe.com/copilot_internal/v2/token   Bearer gho_VICTIM_REFRESH_TOKEN

C. public github.com profile (control)
  persisted enterpriseUrl: (none)
  model routing:  gpt-5 -> https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com
  token refresh:  completed
  requests carrying the credential: 1
    -> https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token   Bearer gho_VICTIM_REFRESH_TOKEN

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
registry lookup getOAuthProvider("github-copilot") -> GitHub Copilot

A. legacy profile minted by an off-allowlist host
  persisted enterpriseUrl: attacker.example
  model routing:  github-copilot withheld, access token has no route
  token refresh:  refused, Refusing to refresh GitHub Copilot token for unsupported enterprise domain "attacker.example". Re-authenticate with a supported host (github.com or a *.ghe.com tenant).
  requests carrying the credential: 0

B. data-residency tenant (control)
  persisted enterpriseUrl: acme.ghe.com
  model routing:  gpt-5 -> https://api.acme.ghe.com
  token refresh:  completed
  requests carrying the credential: 1
    -> https://api.acme.ghe.com/copilot_internal/v2/token   Bearer gho_VICTIM_REFRESH_TOKEN

C. public github.com profile (control)
  persisted enterpriseUrl: (none)
  model routing:  gpt-5 -> https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com
  token refresh:  completed
  requests carrying the credential: 1
    -> https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token   Bearer gho_VICTIM_REFRESH_TOKEN
```
Observed result after fix: on pristine main the off-allowlist profile hands `gho_VICTIM_REFRESH_TOKEN` to `api.attacker.example` and routes `gpt-5` to `https://api.attacker.example`, so the access token reaches that origin even with no refresh; after the patch that same profile issues zero outbound requests and its models are withheld entirely, while the `acme.ghe.com` tenant and the public `github.com` profile keep byte-identical routing and refresh behavior.
What was not tested: no live GitHub or Copilot request was made, the outbound boundary was recorded rather than sent, so no real credential left the process. Recovery is exercised at the doctor-hint and routing level rather than by running an interactive `openclaw onboard --auth-choice github-copilot` re-login end to end. Full `pnpm build` was not run.

target.title: feat(cloud-workers): openclaw worker mode running the embedded loop on the box
target.body:
Part of #104294 (cloud workers, milestone 2, PR 9 — the composition PR). Builds on the four landed milestone-2 backend contracts: #104688 (worker role), #104809 (transcript commits), #105275 (live events), #105719 (inference proxy). Design: `docs/plan/cloud-workers.md` (openclaw worker mode).

## What Problem This Solves

The four backend RPCs exist on the gateway side, but nothing yet runs an agent session ON a worker box. This PR adds `openclaw worker` mode: the entry point + worker-side runtime that dials the gateway over the reverse tunnel, admits with the minted credential + handshake, and runs the embedded agent loop on the box — with its persistence, model, and streaming seams tethered to the gateway, and tools running locally. This is where a worker box becomes capable of running a real session driven from the gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `openclaw worker` entry: restricted runtime (loadPlugins:"never", no channels, no gateway HTTP surfaces, throwaway mkdtemp 0700 state dir, in-memory empty auth storage — no local model auth profile read). Dials the tunnel-forwarded local socket, presents credential + handshake, attaches to its single assigned session. Fails closed on admission failure (with a bounded 120s admission deadline so a leased box can't burn forever on an unreachable gateway).
- Embedded runner rewired: session persistence -> transcript-commit RPC client (base-leaf CAS + runEpoch + seq, durable replay dedupe); model calls -> inference-proxy RPC client (provider/model reference strings only, streamed deltas + terminal, durable-replay resume); streaming -> live-event RPC client (monotonic seq, cumulative ACK, unacked-tail replay). Tools are the six coding tools (read/write/edit/apply_patch/exec/process), local-only, fail-closed availability check.
- Reconnect/resume: exact-frame transcript retry (ledger dedupe), cumulative live-ACK replay of the unacked tail, durable inference resume (single provider call, no double-bill). Owner-epoch supersession -> clean fenced exit. Oversized transcript messages fail closed producer-side.

## Deep-review fixes (a dedicated adversarial review found real concurrency/lifecycle bugs)

- **BLOCKER fixed:** stop() during an in-flight transcript commit spun forever (100% CPU hang on SIGINT/SIGTERM) because the terminal `stopped` state was indistinguishable from a transient interrupt and the commit retry loop treated it as retryable. Introduced a terminal WorkerConnectionStoppedError; retry loops now retry only transient interruptions and rethrow on any terminal state. Stop-in-flight and post-stop emit settle promptly.
- **Blast-radius fixed:** a gateway live-event window reset (a streaming-telemetry cursor reset) used to abort the entire run including a healthy in-flight inference turn. Now: satisfiable resyncs renumber the unacked tail from the gateway's expectedSeq (the gateway explicitly tolerates renumbered replay); an unrecoverable live-seam failure degrades to lossy preview streaming while inference/transcript continue. Live events are preview; they no longer kill the turn.
- **Dead-seam removed + contract documented:** the unused in-process resumeFromBase resync was removed (leaf-only rebasing is unsafe — an unseen transcript mutation means stale inference context). On stale-base-leaf the run fail-stops with an explicit lost-tail lifecycle error and no duplicate commit; relaunch-with-fresh-context is milestone-3 (placement) territory, now documented in docs/cli/worker.md.
- **Hardening:** the worker's session write path is now a real promise-chain mutex (was a pass-through relying on an unguarded serial-emission invariant); bounded admission deadline.

## User Impact

Opt-in only; dispatch/UI (target bar, placement) is milestone 3. This makes a worker box able to run a session end-to-end. No config/changelog/version-bump changes.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: src/worker (runtime, RPC clients, launch), gateway worker-environments, CLI command policy, lint-suppressions — 744 tests green, including the deep-review regression tests (stop-during-commit, resync-below-cursor renumber, live-seam-failure-does-not-abort, stale-base-leaf fail-stop, epoch-flip mid-inference, reconnect-mid-stream single provider call).
- Dedicated adversarial correctness review verified the hard parts correct (CAS/seq/replay dedupe, live ACK math, inference resume/no-double-bill, epoch fencing under withLock, restriction invariants) and found the bugs above, all fixed.
- Clean build (rm -rf dist): public plugin-SDK declaration graph 5,077,853/5,100,000; no [INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]. Type-aware lint, check:test-types, madge + import cycles zero, protocol:check, docs:map:check all green. Codex fresh autoreview clean.

target.title: fix(cli): restore terminal state before exit in logs and hooks commands
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`process.exit(1)` in `logs-cli.ts:685` and `hooks-cli.ts:153` bypasses the CLI's standard exit path (`runtime.exit()`), which calls `restoreTerminalState()` before terminating. This means the terminal state (raw mode, cursor visibility, ANSI reset sequences, active progress line) is not cleaned up when these commands exit on error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every other CLI command uses `runtime.exit()` → `restoreTerminalState()` → `process.exit()` as defined in `src/runtime.ts:89-96`. These two call sites were the only exceptions. A review of the commit history shows no evidence this was intentional — the `process.exit(1)` was introduced during the initial monorepo import and never revisited.

## User Impact

Very low in practice — `logs follow` does not set raw mode itself, and `restoreTerminalState()` operations all have TTY guards. But it is a defensive fix to ensure terminal state is always restored on exit, consistent with the rest of the CLI contract.

## Evidence

- **Contract**: `src/runtime.ts:89-96` — `defaultRuntime.exit()` calls `restoreTerminalState("runtime exit", ...)` before `process.exit()`
- **Consistency**: All other CLI commands (config, plugins-search, devices, gateway run-loop) use `runtime.exit()`
- **Commit history**: `git blame` confirms the raw `process.exit(1)` was added in the initial monorepo import commit with no subsequent discussion or adjustment
- **Tests**: `logs-cli.test.ts` (5/5), `hooks-cli.test.ts` (37/37) — all passing

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/cli/logs-cli.ts` | Import `restoreTerminalState` and call it before `process.exit(1)` on unrecoverable follow error |
| `src/cli/hooks-cli.ts` | Replace `process.exit(1)` with `defaultRuntime.exit(1)` (already imported) |

target.title: fix(config): propagate provider-level contextTokens default to models (#105821)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`models.providers.*.contextTokens` is documented as a provider-level default effective runtime context cap for models under that provider. However, `applyModelDefaults` in `src/config/defaults.ts` only considered per-model `contextTokens`, so models that omitted the field did not inherit the provider default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime already falls back to provider-level `contextTokens` in `applyConfiguredContextWindows`, but config consumers that read the materialized model entries—such as `openclaw models list` and config snapshots—saw `undefined` and omitted the effective cap. This brings `applyModelDefaults` in line with the documented contract and with the existing provider-level `api` default propagation.

## User Impact

Users who set `contextTokens` on a provider will now see the inherited cap reflected for every model under that provider in `openclaw models list` and other config-aware surfaces, unless a model explicitly overrides it.

## Evidence

### Unit tests
Added regression tests in `src/config/model-alias-defaults.test.ts`:

- `propagates provider-level contextTokens default to models` fails before the fix (`contextTokens` is `undefined`) and passes after (`120000`).
- `lets per-model contextTokens override provider-level default` confirms explicit model values still win.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/model-alias-defaults.test.ts --run
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests  20 passed (20)
```

### Real CLI output
Config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, redacted):

```json
{
  "models": {
    "providers": {
      "demo-provider": {
        "baseUrl": "https://demo-provider.example.test/v1",
        "apiKey": "sk-demo-redacted",
        "api": "openai-completions",
        "contextTokens": 120000,
        "models": [
          { "id": "inherited-cap", "name": "Inherited cap model", "contextWindow": 200000, "maxTokens": 8192 },
          { "id": "overridden-cap", "name": "Overridden cap model", "contextWindow": 200000, "maxTokens": 8192, "contextTokens": 96000 }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

After the fix, `openclaw models list --json --no-color` shows the inherited cap on the first model and the explicit override on the second:

```json
{
  "count": 2,
  "models": [
    {
      "key": "demo-provider/inherited-cap",
      "name": "Inherited cap model",
      "input": "text",
      "contextWindow": 200000,
      "contextTokens": 120000,
      "local": false,
      "available": true,
      "tags": ["default"],
      "missing": false
    },
    {
      "key": "demo-provider/overridden-cap",
      "name": "Overridden cap model",
      "input": "text",
      "contextWindow": 200000,
      "contextTokens": 96000,
      "local": false,
      "available": true,
      "tags": [],
      "missing": false
    }
  ]
}
```

Before the fix, the first row omitted `contextTokens` entirely.

Fixes #105821

target.title: fix(safeguard): resolve compaction provider/model before registering runtime
target.body:
Fixes #57901.

## What Problem This Solves

Normal safeguard auto-compaction still registers the active session model even when `agents.defaults.compaction.model` selects a different summarization target. Main's new route-aware auth planner fixed explicit compaction, but normal safeguard registration still ignored the override.

A safeguard override also needs its model route and credential to remain one atomic tuple. Binding a target credential into the active attempt registry can corrupt same-provider sessions before compaction starts.

## Summary

This refresh is merged with main at `266d49cddb977c45d40f13d27045214db29bc756` and adapts the safeguard override to the current route-aware runtime planner.

- Resolve the configured safeguard target before synchronous extension registration.
- Reuse an existing prepared auth plan only when it exactly matches the target provider/model.
- Otherwise prepare the target through the atomic runtime flow:
  `prepareAgentRuntimeAuth` → `materializePreparedRuntimeModel` → `resolvePreparedRuntimeAuthAttempts` → `resolvePreparedRuntimeModelAuth`.

target.title: fix(proxy-capture): honor response backpressure and client abort
target.body:
Closes #105701

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the debug proxy capture server would forward upstream response bodies without honoring `ServerResponse.write()` backpressure, and could crash or leave work running when a client aborted mid-stream. Operators and test fixtures using the debug proxy could see unbounded memory growth under slow clients and unhandled write errors on disconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

The HTTP response forward path uses Node native `Readable.pipe()` for backpressure, keeps body-preview capture as an independent `data` observer, cancels upstream on client abort, and preserves pre-header 502 / post-header abort behavior on upstream errors. Existing partial-upstream-error behavior (complete 502 before headers / abort after headers) is preserved.

## User Impact

Debug proxy traffic capture remains available for local diagnostics and fixture recording, but slow clients no longer force unbounded buffering of upstream response data, and mid-response client aborts no longer leave the proxy in a fragile write-after-end state. No product config or user-facing channel behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Verification host:** local macOS (agent; CS option 1 follow-up)

Commands run after native-pipe refactor:

```text
pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.ts src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# pass

pnpm exec oxlint src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.ts src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# 0 warnings / 0 errors

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# 9/9 passed

# Real proxy process proof (origin + startDebugProxyServer in-process listeners,
# real HTTP clients over loopback — not unit Fake streams):
# slow client pause-after-first-chunk, mid-response abort, subsequent /healthy
```

Focused tests:
- native pipe backpressure + capture observer
- client abort destroys upstream
- mid-response abort + later healthy request through same proxy

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Debug proxy forwards upstream bodies via Node native `Readable.pipe()` backpressure; preview capture is an independent `data` observer; client abort cancels upstream; later requests still succeed.
- Environment: local macOS, branch tip after CS follow-up commit, Node via `pnpm exec tsx` / `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: main ignored `write()` false (no backpressure). First PR revision used a hand-written pause/drain controller; CS asked for native pipe + real-process proof.
- Exact steps after this patch:
  1. Refactor `pipeUpstreamBodyToClient` to `upstreamRes.pipe(res)` with capture observer + abort cancel.
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts` → 9/9.
  3. Real-process proof: start streaming origin + `startDebugProxyServer` listeners; HTTP client slow-read; abort after first chunk; GET `/healthy` on same proxy.
- Evidence after fix (redacted loopback ports):

```text
[proof] origin listening on 127.0.0.1:65525
[proof] proxy process server listening on http://127.0.0.1:65526
[proof] step1: slow client through real proxy
[proof] slow client: pausing reads for 200ms after first chunk
[proof] step1 done: status=200 chunks=202 bodyBytes=1905 aborted=false
[proof] step2: mid-response client abort
[proof] client abort after first chunk (8 bytes)
[proof] step2 done: aborted=true chunks=1
[proof] step3: subsequent healthy request on same proxy
[proof] step3 done: status=200 body="ok" complete=true
[proof] PASS: real proxy survived slow client + abort and served later request
```

- Control check: unit suite still covers capture + abort destroy; vitest 9/9 green; oxlint/oxfmt clean on touched files.
- Observed result: slow client completed; abort cancelled mid-stream; subsequent healthy returned 200 `ok` on the same proxy.
- What was not tested: CONNECT tunnel backpressure (still socket pipe), multi-GB responses, non-macOS hosts, full-repo CI.

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human operator owns the contributor fork push and PR submission policy for this pipeline.

## What Problem This Solves

Closes #105820

When a provider config sets `contextTokens` (the effective runtime context cap),
`applyModelDefaults` did not propagate it to model entries that omit the field.
Models showed no effective cap, and `openclaw models list` omitted the cap for
those models, even though the runtime (`applyConfiguredContextWindows`) already
falls back to the provider value.

## Evidence

```
model.contextTokens === undefined  // provider set 120000, but model didn't inherit it
```

**After** — model inherits provider-level contextTokens:
```
model.contextTokens === 120000  // inherited from provider config
```

**Tests** (3 new + 18 existing = 21 pass):
```
 ✓ inherits provider-level contextTokens when model omits it
 ✓ lets per-model contextTokens override provider-level default
 ✓ leaves contextTokens undefined when neither model nor provider set it
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The documentation in `docs/gateway/config-tools.md` says provider-level
`contextTokens` sets a default effective runtime context cap for models
under that provider. Runtime (`src/agents/context.ts`) already falls back
to the provider value, but `applyModelDefaults` in `src/config/defaults.ts`
never read it. This caused config snapshots and `openclaw models list` to
show no effective cap.

## Merge Risk

Low — 9-line change in `src/config/defaults.ts` plus 3 targeted tests.
Per-model `contextTokens` still takes precedence over the provider default;
when neither is set, behavior is unchanged (undefined).

target.title: fix(doctor): filter informational SQLite migration warnings from startup preflight
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103545 — Gateway startup fails when SQLite migration target already exists for Matrix state.

When the shared SQLite state store already contains data from previous Matrix migrations (storage metadata, sync cache, recovery key, IndexedDB snapshot, legacy crypto migration), the gateway startup preflight treats informational "Skipped ... because SQLite already has ..." messages as fatal errors. This blocks startup for users with pre-migrated Matrix state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Matrix "SQLite already has data" messages are informational — the migration target already exists and the legacy source is safely archived. These are idempotent skips, not data conflicts. Moving them from `warnings` to `notices` uses the existing `PluginDoctorStateMigration` return type field and keeps them visible to operators without blocking startup.

**Scope is intentionally limited to Matrix.** Other extensions were considered but intentionally excluded:

- **Memory Core**: `targetHasRows` uses `.some(Boolean)` across namespaces, so one populated namespace skips the entire legacy source. This can leave partial migration state and should remain a blocking warning.
- **Workboard**: The differing-value case runs only after `JSON.stringify` comparison failed, meaning the SQLite value conflicts with the legacy value. This is a real data conflict and should remain a blocking warning.

## Changes

| Extension | Messages moved | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Matrix | 5 ("because SQLite already has ...") | `doctor-contract-api.ts` |

Tests updated in `extensions/matrix/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` to assert `notices` for the moved messages.

## User Impact

Users with legacy Matrix state that has already been migrated to SQLite can now start the gateway successfully. The informational notices still appear in the "Doctor notices" output, so operators can see that migrations were skipped — they just no longer block startup.

## Evidence

- [x] `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` — 6/6 passed

target.title: fix(memory): skip placeholder short-term promotions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #80582.

Short-term memory promotion could treat markdown and QMD scaffolding as durable content. That included empty list/checklist/fence/table fragments, placeholder daily-note headings, generic daily/dreaming headings, QMD hunk wrappers, collapsed persisted heading prefixes, and mixed snippets that carried structural text alongside real content.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix centralizes short-term snippet promotability in the promotion resolver and applies that resolver across recall recording, store normalization, grounded candidates, ranking, relocation/rehydration, and direct promotion application.

Placeholder-only snippets are skipped. Mixed snippets keep real content while dropping structural wrappers such as QMD hunk headers, generic daily/dreaming headings, collapsed heading prefixes, and bullet-prefixed collapsed heading prefixes. Ordinary non-generic bullets remain intact.

The diagnostic skipped recall event now has an additive `unpromotable-short-term-snippet` reason, with the Plugin SDK API baseline hash regenerated for the exported event type change.

## User Impact

Memory promotion should carry actual remembered content instead of daily-note scaffolding or QMD placeholder text. Existing meaningful snippets still promote, and legacy event readers continue to read recorded recall events while diagnostic readers can see skipped recall records.

target.title: fix(webchat): strip U+2800-U+28FF braille glyphs from usage line
target.body:
Fixes #105481.

## What Problem This Solves

In WebChat (and TUI, which routes through the same message pipeline) every
non-empty tool output — `exec`, `read`, `fetch`, `write`, etc. — renders as an
inline **image attachment** instead of text once an agent turn completes.
Users lose visibility of every tool result and the agent becomes effectively
unusable in the affected session; the only workaround so far has been wiping
the session cache and manually stripping U+2800-U+28FF from dist JS on every
gateway restart.

## Root cause

The default usage-bar template
(`src/auto-reply/usage-bar/default-template.ts`) uses a **braille meter
scale** — `"⠐⡀⡄⡆⡇⣇⣧⣷⣿"` (U+2800-U+28FF) — to render the context-usage bar in
the per-turn footer (e.g. `📚[⣿⣿⣿⣧⠐]128k`).

`resolveResponseUsageLine` returns that rendered footer, and
`appendUsageLine` concatenates it onto the last text payload before delivery,
so any tool output that ends the turn inherits the braille bar.

In the WebChat rendering pipeline, markdown-it's downstream renderer
interprets any U+2800-U+28FF codepoint as a **binary / image sentinel** — the
Uint16 code unit for U+2800 collides with markdown-it's binary-content marker
— so the moment a braille glyph enters the outbound payload, the whole
message is treated as a binary blob and rendered as an inline image
attachment instead of markdown text.

The reporter's temporary workaround
(`re.sub(r'[\u2800-\u28FF]','', …)` over dist JS) confirmed the codepoint
range; gateway restart recompiles from source and reintroduces the glyphs,
which pointed straight at the usage-bar template as the only in-tree emitter
of U+2800-U+28FF into user-visible outbound text.

## Fix

Strip U+2800-U+28FF codepoints from the resolved usage line at the same
boundary in `resolveResponseUsageLine` that already picks between the
rendered usage bar and the plain `Usage: X in / Y out` fallback — but **only
when the target channel is `webchat`**. Discord, Telegram, iMessage, Matrix,
Signal, TUI-over-native-terminal, etc. keep the braille bar unchanged; they
render braille codepoints correctly.

The fix is intentionally narrow:

- No template mutation — clients that override `messages.usageTemplate` with
  their own braille layout still get scrubbed uniformly on WebChat.
- No changes to `appendUsageLine` — reply payload metadata and transcript
  mirrors are untouched.
- No new dependency on the terminal-core `sanitizeTerminalText` helper, which
  is a different sanitizer (single-line control-char stripper for logs).

Diff summary:

```
 .../reply/agent-runner-usage-line.test.ts          | 49 +++++++++++++++++++++-
 src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-usage-line.ts    | 24 +++++++++--
 2 files changed, 69 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

## Evidence

Focused vitest run against the changed file
(`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-usage-line.test.ts`, using the repo's
existing `unit-fast` project — no full `pnpm build`/CI locally):

```
 ✓ unit-fast  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-usage-line.test.ts (3 tests) 3ms
   ✓ appendUsageLine > preserves reply payload metadata when appending usage text
   ✓ resolveResponseUsageLine — braille glyph scrubbing for WebChat
     > strips U+2800–U+28FF braille glyphs from the usage line when channel is webchat
   ✓ resolveResponseUsageLine — braille glyph scrubbing for WebChat
     > keeps braille glyphs intact on non-webchat channels (discord, tui)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The two new regression tests assert both halves of the fix:

1. `channel: "webchat"` — the resolved usage line must not contain any
   U+2800-U+28FF codepoint. Before the fix this failed with the rendered
   footer containing `⣿⣿⣿⣧⠐` from the braille meter.
2. `channel: "discord"` — the resolved usage line still contains
   U+2800-U+28FF, confirming other surfaces are not regressed.

Local repro against the pre-fix source rendered the footer as
`... 📚[⣿⣿⣿⣧⠐]128k 💰0.0002`; after the fix the same call on `webchat`
returns `... 📚[]128k 💰0.0002` (bar collapsed to empty brackets, meter
glyphs gone, no image-attachment corruption in WebChat).

Full CI (typecheck / lint / build / cross-file tests) was **not** run locally
per repo TOOLS.md constraints (no pnpm-driven full test); relying on GitHub
Actions to catch any wider fallout.

target.title: fix(tool-call-repair): parse JSON-format plain-text tool calls alongside bracket/XML/Harmony
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model emits tool calls as plain JSON text (e.g. `{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "Paris"}}`) instead of through the native `tool_calls` response field, OpenClaw's plain-text tool-call repair fails to promote it into an executable tool call. The parser only recognized bracket (`[name]`), XML (`<function=>`), and Harmony formats.

Additionally, three related gaps fixed:

- **Multi-call truncation**: JSON `tool_calls` wrapper parser only read `toolCalls[0]`, dropping subsequent entries
- **Overly broad stripping**: Without shape validation, ordinary JSON prose was removed from visible text
- **Name-only false positives**: `{"name":"read","status":"ok"}` miscategorized as tool call

Affects Ollama, LM Studio, xAI via `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper`. Observed with Qwen family models.

Fixes #99251

## Why This Change Was Made

**Payload parser** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts`):
- `readJsonToolName`, `hasJsonToolArgs`, `readJsonToolArguments` — multi-field name/args extraction
- `extractJsonToolCallNameAndArgs` returns array — multi-tool wrappers promote all valid entries
- Atomic wrapper rejection: any malformed entry → entire `tool_calls` array rejected
- Non-record argument rejection: arrays/strings/primitives rejected, not coerced
- `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` — scans `{`, validates via `JSON.parse`, requires tool-call shape
- Pre-scan gate: `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` disables JSON stripping when mixed with prose
- Exported `scanJsonObject` and `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` for stream normalizer reuse

**Stream normalizer** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.ts`):
- `looksLikeJsonToolCall` — shape heuristic validates buffered JSON after completion
- `findPotentialCallStart` — accepts any line-start `{` as a candidate, even before the shape key is visible (e.g. `{"na`). `classifyPending` holds incomplete JSON and validates/replays once the object completes
- `classifyPending` JSON pre-check — `scanJsonObject` tracks structural depth; shape-key validation (`looksLikeJsonToolCall` + `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt`) deferred until the JSON object closes. False positives (non-tool JSON prose) replay as visible text
- Aligned with bracket/XML/Harmony patterns: stream-time withhold + terminal promotion
- **Revision 5 (1a2e9f3)**: Removed premature shape-key gate from `findPotentialCallStart`. Previously a chunk ending before or inside the quoted key (e.g. `{"na`) fell through as visible text while the completed terminal snapshot was still promoted, causing raw-JSON-plus-tool double delivery. Now any line-start `{` starts a candidate; `classifyPending` defers validation until the JSON object completes.

## User Impact

- Models returning JSON tool calls in `content` now execute tools correctly
- Multi-tool wrappers promote all entries, not just the first
- Ordinary JSON prose preserved; name-only JSON not falsely classified
- Streamed bare JSON tool-call objects are withheld from visible text from the first `{`, eliminating the "see raw JSON then tool executes" double-delivery defect regardless of stream chunk boundaries

## Evidence

### Unit tests — all passing
```
packages/tool-call-repair:             3 files, 164 tests passed
src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts:   1 file,  62 tests passed
```

### New regression tests (28 total in payload + stream-normalizer)
Key invariants:
- **Split before shape key** (`{"na` → rest): buffered entirely, zero `text_delta` leak
- **Split inside shape key** (`{"name` → rest): buffered entirely, zero `text_delta` leak
- **3-way split** before key + mid-object: no leak at any chunk boundary
- **Split before key + terminal done**: promoted to tool call, no raw JSON in text_delta
- Non-tool-call JSON prose (`{"status":"ok"}`) yielded as visible text
- Name-only JSON (`{"name":"read","status":"ok"}`) yielded as visible text
- Plain JSON object without tool shape yielded as visible text
- `tool_calls` wrapper buffered across multiple chunks
- Non-tool-call JSON replayed as false-positive at done
- Visible prefix before a line-start JSON tool call preserved

### Real behavior proof — DeepSeek API live validation

**Scenario 1 — Standalone JSON tool call parsed and stripped**
```
Model output: {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "北京"}}
parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt: ✅ 1 tool call, name=get_weather, args={"city":"北京"}
stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks: ✅ raw JSON fully removed (not delivered to user)
```

**Scenario 2 — Ordinary JSON not misidentified**
```
Model output: {"timeout": 30, "retries": 3}
parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt: ✅ 0 tool calls (correctly ignored)
→ ordinary JSON remains visible in prose
```

**Scenario 3 — Mixed content (ordinary JSON + tool call)**
```
Model output: 系统配置 {"timeout": 30}
{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "上海"}}
Tool-call line → ✅ correctly parsed as get_weather tool call
Config JSON line → ✅ correctly ignored (ordinary JSON visible)
```

**Scenario 4 — Live agent regression check**
```
$ pnpm build && pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main_assistant \
    --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --message "北京现在什么天气？"
```
- ✅ Agent completed with stopReason=stop, 2 tool calls executed (web_search, web_fetch)
- ✅ `finalAssistantVisibleText` clean — no raw JSON leaked to visible output
- ✅ No crash/error in stream pipeline, replay invalid=false

Provider tested: **DeepSeek** (deepseek-v4-pro, via OpenClaw bundled deepseek plugin)
Proof methodology: Real API calls → parse + strip verification → live agent regression
Evidence artifacts: Terminal output captured 2026-07-13, commit 1a2e9f3

### Lint & format
```
oxlint → clean
pnpm format:check → clean
```

### Branch
Rebased onto upstream/main (2026-07-12), no conflicts.

### ClawSweeper rank-up moves addressed (all 5 revisions)
- [P1] JSON-aware stream buffering (looksLikeJsonToolCall + classifyPending pre-check)
- [P2] Multi-call tool_calls array promotion (all entries, not just first)
- [P1] JSON shape validation before stripping (parseJsonToolCallBlockEndAt)
- [P2] UTF-8 byte limit enforcement in parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt
- [P1] Buffer JSON before shape key is complete — `findPotentialCallStart` accepts any line-start `{`; `classifyPending` defers validation (revision 5, 1a2e9f3)

### ClawSweeper proof guidance satisfied
- [P1] **Real provider trace**: DeepSeek API returning JSON-format tool calls, verified through all 4 parse/strip/live-agent scenarios above
- [P1] **One valid JSON tool call executes once**: ✅ Scenario 1 confirms parse + strip → one clean promotion
- [P1] **Raw JSON not delivered**: ✅ stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks removes raw JSON; agent live run shows clean visible text
- [P1] **Ordinary JSON remains visible**: ✅ Scenario 2/3 confirm non-tool JSON is preserved in prose

target.title: fix: guard optional-chain results with nullish coalescing before non-optional method calls
target.body:
## Summary

Optional-chain results (`?.map()`, `?.filter()`) short-circuit to `undefined`, causing `TypeError` crashes when non-optional methods (`.map()`, `.filter()`, `.join()`, `.trim()`) are chained immediately after. This PR wraps every affected optional-chain result with `?? []` before the non-optional chain, or extends the optional chain for string-producing paths.

- Problem: `value?.map(fn).filter(fn)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')` when `value` is `undefined`, because `?.map()` returns `undefined` and `.filter()` is called on it.
- Solution: Insert `?? []` between the optional chain and the non-optional chain: `(value?.map(fn) ?? []).filter(fn)`. For string-producing paths, use `?.join() ?? ""`.
- What changed:
  - `src/gateway/node-pairing-ssh-verify.ts` — wrap `cfg.cidrs?.map()` with `?? []` before `.filter()`
  - `src/gateway/node-pairing-auto-approve.ts` — wrap `params.autoApproveCidrs?.map()` with `?? []` before `.filter()`
  - `src/acp/translator.ts` — wrap `content?.filter()` with `?? []` before `.map()` (2 sites)
  - `src/acp/client.ts` — extend optional chain: `?.map()?.join() ?? ""`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/current-turn-images.ts` — wrap `ctx.MediaUnderstanding?.filter()` with `?? []` before `.map()`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-diagnostics.ts` — wrap `result.content?.map()` with `?? []` before `.filter()`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-export-trajectory.ts` — same pattern
  - `src/crestodian/agent-turn.ts` — wrap `result.payloads?.map()` with `?? []` before `.filter()`
  - `src/crestodian/setup-inference.ts` — same pattern
  - `src/crestodian/assistant.ts` — same pattern
  - `src/commitments/runtime.ts` — wrap `result.payloads?.map()` with `?? []` before `.filter()`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/tool-media-payloads.ts` — wrap `params.toolMediaUrls?.map()` with `?? []` before `.filter()`
- What did NOT change: No behavioral changes on the happy path. When the optional-chain subject is a valid array, the `?? []` is a no-op and the chain produces identical results.

## Change Type & Scope

### Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

### Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related to #104980
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Thirteen call sites across the codebase chain non-optional array methods immediately after an optional chain. When the optional chain short-circuits to `undefined`, the process throws a `TypeError`. The highest-impact sites are in gateway node pairing — setting `sshVerify: true` or triggering auto-approve without `autoApproveCidrs` configured crashes the gateway deterministically. The remaining sites affect agent content streaming, diagnostics commands, trajectory export, crestodian inference, and commitment extraction.

## Review Contract

```text
Ref: #104980
Surface: gateway / agents / auto-reply / crestodian / commitments

Bug: Optional-chain result (undefined) fed directly to non-optional array method calls causes TypeError crashes.
Cause: `?.map()`/`?.filter()` short-circuits to `undefined` when the subject is nullish; subsequent
  `.map()`/`.filter()`/`.join()`/`.trim()` calls throw because they operate on `undefined`, not `[]`.
  In every case the surrounding code already handles empty/missing values gracefully — it just
  never gets the chance because the crash happens first.
Provenance:
  introduced by: recent development (2026-07-09 / 2026-07-10), commits fc463e3b61a and 58b0ec9e50fd
  made visible by: main branch at 4139938dcf1
  置信度: clear

Best fix: Each site is fixed by inserting `?? []` to convert the optional-chain result to a safe
  empty array before non-optional chaining. This is the minimal, safest fix — it preserves the
  happy path exactly and only changes behavior when the value is absent, which is the crash case.
Refactor: No — each fix is a single-expression mechanical change. The pattern could be linted
  globally but that is out of scope for this PR.
Proof: source analysis + type-level verification
Risk: Low. The `?? []` fallback produces identical results to the existing `?? []` guards already
  present at several sites (they were just placed too late in the chain). The only behavioral
  change is converting a crash into a graceful empty result.
```

## Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: TypeError crash when optional-chain subject is `undefined`/`null` and non-optional array methods follow.

**Real environment tested**: N/A — this is a defensive null-safety fix. The fixes are mechanical: each site adds `?? []` or `?.` at the exact point where `undefined` could leak into a non-optional method call. TypeScript's type system does not flag this pattern because `?.method()` returns `T | undefined` and the non-optional chain is typed against `T`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Build check
pnpm build
# Type check
pnpm tsgo
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
# Before: cfg.cidrs?.map(fn).filter(fn) — crashes when cidrs is undefined
# After: (cfg.cidrs?.map(fn) ?? []).filter(fn) — returns [] when cidrs is undefined

# Before: content?.filter(fn).map(fn).join("\n").trimEnd() — crashes when content is undefined
# After: (content?.filter(fn) ?? []).map(fn).join("\n").trimEnd() — returns "" when content is undefined
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- All 13 sites now safely produce empty results (`[]`, `""`, or `undefined`) instead of throwing when the optional-chain subject is absent
- Happy-path behavior unchanged: when the subject is a valid array, `?? []` is a no-op

**What was not tested**:

- Live gateway node pairing with `sshVerify: true` (requires real companion app + device)
- Live ACP content streaming with missing `content` in delta events (requires specific upstream ACP server behavior)
- These are defensive fixes — the crash scenarios are deterministic given the input shapes

### Verification environment

- OS: Linux
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/optional-chain-crashes-104980

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: The crestodian `extractRunText` sites (3 copies) — the original `??` chain returns the third alternative when the first two are nullish. With the fix, if `payloads` is `undefined`, the `?? []` fallback produces `[].filter(Boolean).join("\n")` = `""`, which is not nullish, so the outer `??` chain returns `""` instead of falling through. This changes `extractRunText` from returning `undefined` to `""` when payloads is absent. Callers already handle empty strings via `?.trim()` so this is safe.
- **Mitigation**: Each fix follows the identical mechanical pattern already used correctly elsewhere in the codebase.
- **Compatibility impact**: None — no API, config, or storage changes.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: All 13 sites compile without type errors; oxfmt formatting passes on all modified files.
- **Edge cases checked**: `undefined` input, empty array input, populated array input — all produce correct results.
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live gateway node pairing flow, live ACP streaming, live crestodian inference. These require real device/app infrastructure.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Identified all sites via `git grep` for `?.map(.*)\.(map|filter|join|trim)` and `?.filter(.*)\.(map|filter|join|trim)` patterns across `src/`. Applied mechanical `?? []` insertion at each site. Verified operator precedence required wrapping parentheses around the optional-chain expression before `?? []`.

Fixes #104980

AI-assisted with Codex. I reviewed the implementation and the live proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running a local agent with `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` could receive an immediate HTTP 413 for even a one-word prompt on Groq's 12,000 TPM base tier. The default agent request combined the model's full 32,768-token output capability with the normal prompt and tool schemas, making the request too large before generation began.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Groq plugin leaves the normal first request unchanged. Only a specifically matched Groq HTTP 413 `Request too large` TPM rejection is retried once with tool fields removed and a 1,024-token output limit. The fallback mutation runs after configured payload hooks so they cannot restore the rejected request shape. Explicit max-token overrides skip this recovery policy. Synchronous transport failures retain their normal throw semantics, while asynchronous pre-stream failures retain complete model metadata. The change stays provider- and model-scoped instead of changing shared OpenAI-compatible transport behavior or hard-coding an account's TPM tier as the model capability.

PR #104916 is a competing broader fix that omits implicit output reservations across most OpenAI-compatible transports. These approaches should not both land: this PR intentionally chooses the narrower Groq/model/error-scoped recovery because it has real-provider proof and avoids changing successful requests for other providers.

## User Impact

Default local-agent turns with `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` can recover on Groq's base tier instead of failing immediately. Higher-limit organizations retain the existing implicit output budget and normal tool-capable first request, while affected base-tier requests retry with the smaller tool-free payload. Other Groq models and explicitly budgeted requests are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before, on current `main`, the exact isolated local-agent flow returned HTTP 413: Groq reported `Limit 12000, Requested 61830` for the one-word prompt `你好`.
- The recovery path was live-proven against Groq: the default command first received the narrowly matched HTTP 413, immediately retried without tool fields, and returned HTTP 200 in the same agent attempt. Groq reported 10,071 input tokens and 452 output tokens (10,523 total).
- On the current fallback-only head, a fresh ordinary request reached Groq with its existing implicit budget (`Requested 64910`), proving the first request is not capped at 1,024. Groq then returned an unrelated daily-quota HTTP 429, and OpenClaw correctly made no recovery request. The account reported that the daily quota will reset in about eight hours, so a second successful live recovery could not be run immediately.
- An explicit 128-token budget with the `session_status` tool also returned HTTP 200. Groq reported 8,860 input tokens and 6 output tokens (8,866 total), and the live system-prompt report retained `session_status`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/groq` — 5 tests passed, including a successful ordinary first request retaining `max_completion_tokens: 32768` and tools, a matching 413 retry canonicalized to only `max_completion_tokens: 1024` when an existing hook tries to restore either or both token aliases plus tools, configured and request-scoped explicit-budget preservation, non-recovery for unrelated 400/401/413-context/429 errors, synchronous throw preservation, and complete asynchronous error metadata.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/groq/index.test.ts` — clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` — clean.
- `node scripts/check-extension-package-tsc-boundary.mjs --help` — all 119 plugin package boundaries compiled, including Groq, plus both canaries.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/groq/index.ts extensions/groq/index.test.ts` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

target.title: fix(doctor): filter informational SQLite migration warnings from startup preflight
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103545 — Gateway startup fails when SQLite migration target already exists for Matrix state.

When the shared SQLite state store already contains data from previous Matrix migrations (storage metadata, sync cache, recovery key, IndexedDB snapshot, legacy crypto migration), the gateway startup preflight treats informational "Skipped ... because SQLite already has ..." messages as fatal errors. This blocks startup for users with pre-migrated Matrix state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Matrix "SQLite already has data" messages are informational — the migration target already exists and the legacy source is safely archived. These are idempotent skips, not data conflicts. Moving them from `warnings` to `notices` uses the existing `PluginDoctorStateMigration` return type field and keeps them visible to operators without blocking startup.

**Scope is intentionally limited to Matrix.** Other extensions were considered but intentionally excluded:

- **Memory Core**: `targetHasRows` uses `.some(Boolean)` across namespaces, so one populated namespace skips the entire legacy source. This can leave partial migration state and should remain a blocking warning.
- **Workboard**: The differing-value case runs only after `JSON.stringify` comparison failed, meaning the SQLite value conflicts with the legacy value. This is a real data conflict and should remain a blocking warning.

## Changes

| Extension | Messages moved | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Matrix | 5 ("because SQLite already has ...") | `doctor-contract-api.ts` |

Tests updated in `extensions/matrix/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` to assert `notices` for the moved messages.

## User Impact

Users with legacy Matrix state that has already been migrated to SQLite can now start the gateway successfully. The informational notices still appear in the "Doctor notices" output, so operators can see that migrations were skipped — they just no longer block startup.

## Evidence

- [x] `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` — 6/6 passed
- [x] No changes to `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts` needed — `noteStartupStateMigrationResult` already passes the full result to `noteStateMigrationResult` which displays notices; only `startupMigrationWarnings` comes from `result.warnings`

target.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint after inbound admission gates pass. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

When the first cold turn has no stored thread session entry yet, the monitor records a pending backfill marker and adopts it once `recordInboundSessionMeta` creates the stored session id. That keeps the marker stable for same-session follow-ups and failed-fetch no-retry, without blocking a later real session-id rotation.

Recovery is now bounded on three axes flagged in review:

- **Thread response size.** `fetchMattermostThreadPosts` requests only the newest `historyLimit + 1` posts via `?perPage=<limit>&direction=up`, then restores ascending chronological order. `GET /posts/{id}/thread` returns the entire thread at the Mattermost default (`perPage=0`), so an unbounded thread would otherwise allocate and parse on the inbound path. The endpoint reads camelCase `perPage` (not `per_page`), so the limit is actually applied.
- **Marker lifecycle.** Backfill tracking uses one marker per thread history key (`Map<historyKey, sessionId>`) instead of a process-lifetime `Set` of `historyKey:session` compound keys. A plugin-local 1000-key LRU cap (`evictOldThreadBackfillMarkers`, matching the `channelHistories` window size) keeps the marker map from outgrowing the history window it accompanies; the cap stays in the plugin rather than touching core history internals. An evicted thread simply re-backfills on its next cold inbound turn. The stored session id is read only after the admission gates, so dropped pre-admission posts never touch the session store.
- **Concurrent cold turns.** Under the default zero-debounce config, two first cold-thread messages can overlap on the awaited thread-history fetch. The first turn sets the completed-attempt marker and publishes a per-history-key in-flight promise; an overlapping same-session turn now awaits that one bounded fetch instead of seeing the marker and skipping into a context-free reply. The in-flight handle is cleared once the fetch settles, so afterward the marker alone governs the intentional one-attempt-per-session no-retry.

## User Impact

Mattermost thread replies keep useful prior context after restart or `/new`, without repeated thread-history requests, unbounded thread fetches, or unbounded per-session marker growth on long-lived monitors. Concurrent first cold-thread messages under zero-debounce no longer race into a context-free reply.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts`: **3 files, 115 passed**. Covers stored thread `sessionId` rotation, same-session no-refetch, failed-fetch no-retry, dropped pre-admission posts, adopt-pending-marker without blocking later rotation, the initially-missing session entry path, marker-map eviction, and the new concurrent-turn deferred-fetch case.
- `oxlint` (repo binary) on the changed prod + test files: **passed**. `tsgo --noEmit -p extensions/mattermost/tsconfig.json`: **passed**.
- Bounded fetch asserted (`client.test.ts`): a limited call issues `?perPage=2&direction=up` and re-sorts ascending so callers still build history oldest-first.
- Bounded marker asserted (`monitor.test.ts`): the backfill requests `historyLimit + 1`, `threadBackfillMarkers.get(historyKey)` carries the current session marker across the rotation / no-refetch / no-retry / adopt paths, and the eviction test drives 1001 distinct threads to prove the marker map stays capped at 1000 (plugin-local LRU), the oldest key is evicted, and an evicted thread with a cold window re-backfills from the server.
- Concurrency asserted (`monitor.test.ts`): with the first cold fetch gated open, an overlapping same-session turn stays pending until that fetch releases, exactly one server fetch runs, both turns observe the recovered window, and the in-flight handle is cleared afterward so the marker governs no-retry.
- Rebased onto latest `origin/main` (0 behind). The only conflict was two independent `describe` blocks colliding in `client.test.ts` (`createMattermostDirectChannelWithRetry delay cap` from main and `fetchMattermostThreadPosts` from this branch); both were kept. Earlier exact-head repairs remain: the thread query uses Mattermost's documented camelCase `perPage` so the response bound is applied, and the chronological re-sort uses non-mutating `toSorted()` to satisfy the bundled-extension `unicorn/no-array-sort` lint lane.

Live proof: local Docker Mattermost Team Edition 10.11.21 at `http://localhost:8065`, with tokens and Mattermost ids redacted. The proof used real Mattermost REST auth, posts, and `/api/v4/posts/<root>/thread` through `monitorMattermostProvider`; a fake websocket only injected `posted` events into the monitor. The route/thread session key stayed stable while the stored thread `sessionId` rotated. Cold start included prior root/thread context, same-session server-only context stayed absent, and stored-thread-session reset included new server-only prior context:

```json
{
  "mattermost": "10.11.21 local Docker, token/id redacted",
  "routeSessionKey": "stable, redacted",
  "threadSessionKey": "stable, redacted",
  "threadSessionKeyStable": true,
  "storedThreadSessionIds": [
    "stored-session-before-reset",
    "stored-session-after-reset"
  ],
  "dispatchCount": 3,
  "firstColdStartContainsPriorThreadContext": true,
  "firstColdStartContainsRootContext": true,
  "sameSessionSkippedServerOnlyContext": true,
  "storedThreadSessionIdResetContainsNewPriorContext": true
}
```
